<script>
  (function () {
    try {
      const match = document.cookie.match(/(?:^|;\s*)bp_userdata=([^;]*)/);
      let user = null;
      if (match && match[1]) {
        const raw = decodeURIComponent(match[1]).replace(/^"|"$/g, '');
        user = JSON.parse(decodeURIComponent(atob(raw)));
      }
      const level = String((user && user.subscription_level) || '').toLowerCase();
      const premium = level === 'premium' || level === 'goat';
      document.documentElement.setAttribute(
        'data-nav-auth',
        user ? (premium ? 'premium' : 'free') : 'out'
      );

      // Which desktop Upgrade label is coming, because the two are not the same width:
      // the non-trial branch adds a lock icon and a gap before a longer word. Mirrors
      // resolveTrialAudience() — affiliate, then past-trial, else trial — and every input
      // it needs is already in reach here (`bp_affiliate` is its own cookie; the other two
      // are fields on `bp_userdata`). A premium user gets no CTA at all, so no attribute.
      if (!premium) {
        const affiliate =
          /(?:^|;\s*)bp_affiliate=/.test(document.cookie) || Boolean(user && user.affiliate_code);
        const wide = affiliate || Boolean(user && user.has_past_trial);
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-nav-upgrade-label', wide ? 'premium' : 'trial');
      }
    } catch (e) {
      /* leave it unset: every placeholder paints, i.e. the pre-existing behaviour */
    }

    // Separate try/catch, because localStorage throws outright in some privacy modes and a
    // failure here must not cost us the cookie-derived audience above. nav/GetStarted exits
    // on EITHER a signed-in user or this flag, so a logged-out visitor who already finished
    // onboarding gets no CTA and must not be shown a placeholder for one.
    try {
      if (localStorage.getItem('bp_onboarding_completed') === 'true') {
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-nav-onboarded', 'true');
      }
    } catch (e) {
      /* same fail-open: no attribute, placeholder paints */
    }
  })();
</script>

Let's get to the top first touchdown scorer predictions for Week 5.</p>

<h2 class="article-content__heading"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/picks/prop-bets/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" src="https://www.bettingpros.com/img/PBCS.jpg/0x0.webp" alt="BettingPros Prop Bet Cheat Sheet" width="1920" height="1080" class="article-content__img aligncenter wp-image-300539 size-full" srcset="https://www.bettingpros.com/img/PBCS.jpg/0x0.webp 1920w, https://www.bettingpros.com/img/PBCS-300x169.jpg/300x169.webp 300w, https://www.bettingpros.com/img/PBCS-818x460.jpg/818x460.webp 818w, https://www.bettingpros.com/img/PBCS-768x432.jpg/768x432.webp 768w, https://www.bettingpros.com/img/PBCS-1536x864.jpg/1536x864.webp 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1920px) 100vw, 1920px" /></a></h2>
<h2 class="article-content__heading"><strong>NFL Week 5 First Touchdown Scorers Picks & Predictions</strong></h2>
<h3 class="article-content__subheading"><strong>Indianapolis Colts @ Pittsburgh Steelers</strong></h3>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">I'm riding with the hot hand this week. Roman Wilson has scored the first touchdown in each of the Steelers' last two games, and he has a juicy matchup this week. The Colts are awful at defending slot receivers, and I would not be surprised to see Wilson's snap share rise.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Michael Pittman Jr. is expected to miss multiple weeks, so Aaron Rodgers will have to count on DK Metcalf and Wilson. Wilson is second on the team with 24 targets through four weeks, including two red-zone targets. They have allowed the second-most yards per target to slot receivers this season. Wilson should have a solid chance of scoring first for the third consecutive week.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Pick: <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/roman-wilson-wr/touchdown-scored/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Roman Wilson</a> (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">+1500 at DraftKings Sportsbook</a>)</strong></p>
<hr />
<h3 class="article-content__subheading"><strong>Chicago Bears @ Green Bay Packers</strong></h3>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The Bears are still without Caleb Williams, so Tyson Bagent is under center again this week. The offense has turned to the ground game without Williams, and it is working well. They are averaging a league-high 196.3 rushing yards per game.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) is dealing with multiple injuries, keeping him out of practice on Thursday. D'Andre Swift should get the majority of the workload this week without Monangai, and his usual totes if Monangai plays. Monangai has taken over twice this season, but Swift has at least 15 carries in every game. Swift is a solid play to score first against a weak Packers defense.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Pick: <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/dandre-swift/touchdown-scored/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">D'Andre Swift</a> (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">+600 at DraftKings Sportsbook</a>)</strong></p>
<hr />
<h3 class="article-content__subheading"><strong>San Francisco 49ers @ Seattle Seahawks</strong></h3>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Mike Evans has not lost a step with the 49ers. He has two touchdowns on the season and played through a rib injury last week. He finished with five receptions for 76 yards. The Seahawks are a tough matchup, but he could still find the end zone first.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Evans is a tough matchup in the red zone, especially when defenses have to worry about Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle. Purdy is looking to Evans in the red zone, with four targets. Deebo Samuel and Kittle each have five, but Evans should get a crack at the first touchdown in a divisional matchup.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Pick: <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/mike-evans/touchdown-scored/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Mike Evans</a> (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://btng.pro/ybNiYa" target="_blank" rel="noopener">+1250 at BetMGM</a>)</strong></p>
<hr />
<h3 class="article-content__subheading"><strong>Detroit Lions @ Arizona Cardinals</strong></h3>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The total in this game is 54.5, so there should be a lot of points. The Lions allow 31.8 points per game, and the Cardinals allow 29.3, the second- and fourth-most in the league, respectively. Trey McBride may have the best matchup of any player.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The Lions allowed tight ends to score two touchdowns per game in the first three weeks. They only allowed 56 yards to the position last week against the Panthers. McBride is a lot better than any tight end the Panthers have. Jacoby Brissett peppers McBride with targets and should look his way early and often.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Pick: <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/trey-mcbride/touchdown-scored/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Trey McBride</a> (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">+1000 at DraftKings Sportsbook</a>)</strong></p>

I'm riding with the hot hand this week. Roman Wilson has scored the first touchdown in each of the Steelers' last two games, and he has a juicy matchup this week. The Colts are awful at defending slot receivers, and I would not be surprised to see Wilson's snap share rise. 

Michael Pittman Jr. is expected to miss multiple weeks, so Aaron Rodgers will have to count on DK Metcalf and Wilson. Wilson is second on the team with 24 targets through four weeks, including two red-zone targets. They have allowed the second-most yards per target to slot receivers this season. Wilson should have a solid chance of scoring first for the third consecutive week. 

 Pick: Roman Wilson ( +1500 at DraftKings Sportsbook ) 
 

### Chicago Bears @ Green Bay Packers 

The Bears are still without Caleb Williams, so Tyson Bagent is under center again this week. The offense has turned to the ground game without Williams, and it is working well. They are averaging a league-high 196.3 rushing yards per game. 

Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) is dealing with multiple injuries, keeping him out of practice on Thursday. D'Andre Swift should get the majority of the workload this week without Monangai, and his usual totes if Monangai plays. Monangai has taken over twice this season, but Swift has at least 15 carries in every game. Swift is a solid play to score first against a weak Packers defense. 

 Pick: D'Andre Swift ( +600 at DraftKings Sportsbook ) 
 

### San Francisco 49ers @ Seattle Seahawks 

Mike Evans has not lost a step with the 49ers. He has two touchdowns on the season and played through a rib injury last week. He finished with five receptions for 76 yards. The Seahawks are a tough matchup, but he could still find the end zone first. 

Evans is a tough matchup in the red zone, especially when defenses have to worry about Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle. Purdy is looking to Evans in the red zone, with four targets. Deebo Samuel and Kittle each have five, but Evans should get a crack at the first touchdown in a divisional matchup. 

 Pick: Mike Evans ( +1250 at BetMGM ) 
 

### Detroit Lions @ Arizona Cardinals 

The total in this game is 54.5, so there should be a lot of points. The Lions allow 31.8 points per game, and the Cardinals allow 29.3, the second- and fourth-most in the league, respectively. Trey McBride may have the best matchup of any player. 

The Lions allowed tight ends to score two touchdowns per game in the first three weeks. They only allowed 56 yards to the position last week against the Panthers. McBride is a lot better than any tight end the Panthers have. Jacoby Brissett peppers McBride with targets and should look his way early and often. 

 Pick: Trey McBride ( +1000 at DraftKings Sportsbook )

<script>
  const KEY = 'bp_display_mode';

  (function () {
    try {
      const match = document.cookie.match(/(?:^|;\s*)bp_userdata=([^;]*)/);
      let user = null;
      if (match && match[1]) {
        const raw = decodeURIComponent(match[1]).replace(/^"|"$/g, '');
        user = JSON.parse(decodeURIComponent(atob(raw)));
      }
      const level = String((user && user.subscription_level) || '').toLowerCase();
      const premium = level === 'premium' || level === 'goat';
      document.documentElement.setAttribute(
        'data-nav-auth',
        user ? (premium ? 'premium' : 'free') : 'out'
      );

      // Which desktop Upgrade label is coming, because the two are not the same width:
      // the non-trial branch adds a lock icon and a gap before a longer word. Mirrors
      // resolveTrialAudience() — affiliate, then past-trial, else trial — and every input
      // it needs is already in reach here (`bp_affiliate` is its own cookie; the other two
      // are fields on `bp_userdata`). A premium user gets no CTA at all, so no attribute.
      if (!premium) {
        const affiliate =
          /(?:^|;\s*)bp_affiliate=/.test(document.cookie) || Boolean(user && user.affiliate_code);
        const wide = affiliate || Boolean(user && user.has_past_trial);
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-nav-upgrade-label', wide ? 'premium' : 'trial');
      }
    } catch (e) {
      /* leave it unset: every placeholder paints, i.e. the pre-existing behaviour */
    }

    // Separate try/catch, because localStorage throws outright in some privacy modes and a
    // failure here must not cost us the cookie-derived audience above. nav/GetStarted exits
    // on EITHER a signed-in user or this flag, so a logged-out visitor who already finished
    // onboarding gets no CTA and must not be shown a placeholder for one.
    try {
      if (localStorage.getItem('bp_onboarding_completed') === 'true') {
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-nav-onboarded', 'true');
      }
    } catch (e) {
      /* same fail-open: no attribute, placeholder paints */
    }
  })();

<h2 class="article-content__heading article-content__heading article-content__heading article-content__heading article-content__heading article-content__heading"><strong>NFL London Same Game Parlay: Eagles vs. Jaguars (Week 5)</strong></h2>
<p class="article-content__paragraph article-content__paragraph article-content__paragraph article-content__paragraph article-content__paragraph article-content__paragraph"><em>(Odds courtesy of <a class="article-content__anchor article-content__anchor article-content__anchor article-content__anchor article-content__anchor article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">DraftKings Sportsbook</a>)</em></p>
<h3 class="article-content__subheading"><b>Philadelphia Eagles vs. Jacksonville Jaguars </b><b></b></h3>
<ul class="article-content__ul">
<li class="article-content__list-item"><b>Leg 1: <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/will-shipley/rushing-yards/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Will Shipley Under 35.5 Rushing Yards</a> (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">-114</a>)</b></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item"><b>Leg 2: <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/will-shipley/receiving-yards/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Will Shipley 15+ Receiving Yards</a> (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">-135</a>)</b></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item"><b>Leg 3: <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/bhayshul-tuten/rushing-yards/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Bhayshul Tuten 70+ Rushing Yards</a> (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">-101</a>)</b></li>
</ul>
<ul class="article-content__ul"></ul>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">In case you haven't heard, the Eagles' offensive line is in shambles. Lane Johnson just retired, Cam Jurgens was surprisingly traded to Baltimore, and Landon Dickerson is still sidelined. Plus, new starting center Drew Kendall has been ruled out ahead of this week's game. That's four starters along the O-line. </span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">It's a less-than-ideal situation for the offense, anyway, but it gets even worse. Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby are also both out. That means Will Shipley and newly-elevated Dameon Pierce headline the Eagles' backfield. Rushing should be very tough to come by behind that makeshift offensive line. </span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">Let's fade Shipley's rushing yards prop in this situation. The Jaguars have been stout against the run this season. Jacksonville is allowing just 3.3 yards per carry, the second-fewest in the league. The defense is also giving up a league-low 47.5 rushing yards per game to opposing running backs. The Jags are stifling every back in their way, and Shipley has to face them with his shaky line. </span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">However, Shipley could be productive as a pass-catcher. Jacksonville is allowing the second-most receiving yards (48.3) and receptions (6.75) per game to running backs this year. Teams are getting stuffed in the run game and looking to use their RBs on quick passes. The Eagles should take a similar approach, especially since Jalen Hurts won't have much time to drop back and throw. Plus, Shipley has proven pass-catching chops from his days at Clemson.</span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">Meanwhile, the other lead back in this game should be in for a big day. Bhayshul Tuten is averaging 4.6 yards per carry with at least 65 rushing yards in each game. He's gained  73 yards in back-to-back weeks ahead of this matchup. On that note, the Eagles are allowing 106.3 rushing yards per game to opposing RBs, the eighth-highest mark in the league. </span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">The Philly defense has also given up 60+ rushing yards to every opposing lead back it's faced this year. In the past two games, the Eagles allowed 84 yards to D'Andre Swift and 80 to Kyren Williams. Tuten can follow suit, especially in a favorable game flow. Jacksonville could be running it a ton in the second half with a lead, considering the touchdown spread. </span></p>

# NFL Same Game Parlays & Picks: Eagles vs. Jaguars (Week 5)

 

 

 
 by Dan Servodidio 
 | @dan_servodidio 
 | 
 Oct 10, 2026 
 
 
 

 

 
 by Dan Servodidio 
 | @dan_servodidio

 Oct 10, 2026 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 

 
NFL Week 5 continues with an intriguing London game matchup. The Philadelphia Eagles take on the Jacksonville Jaguars from Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, England on Sunday morning. The Jags are 7.5-point favorites with a 41.5 over/under. Let's break down the best   NFL London same game parlay (SGP)   to lock in before kickoff. Check out which NFL picks and player props to include. Good luck. 
 

- More NFL Betting Advice 

- NFL Prop Bet Cheat Sheet 

- Expert NFL Game Picks 

- NFL Betting Strategy 

- Best +EV NFL Picks 
 

 Get instant alerts when a line reaches your target via the BettingPros App 

 

## NFL London Same Game Parlay: Eagles vs. Jaguars (Week 5) 

 (Odds courtesy of  DraftKings Sportsbook ) 

### Philadelphia Eagles vs. Jacksonville Jaguars  

 

- Leg 1: Will Shipley Under 35.5 Rushing Yards ( -114 ) 

- Leg 2: Will Shipley 15+ Receiving Yards ( -135 ) 

- Leg 3: Bhayshul Tuten 70+ Rushing Yards ( -101 ) 
 
 

 In case you haven't heard, the Eagles' offensive line is in shambles. Lane Johnson just retired, Cam Jurgens was surprisingly traded to Baltimore, and Landon Dickerson is still sidelined. Plus, new starting center Drew Kendall has been ruled out ahead of this week's game. That's four starters along the O-line.  

 It's a less-than-ideal situation for the offense, anyway, but it gets even worse. Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby are also both out. That means Will Shipley and newly-elevated Dameon Pierce headline the Eagles' backfield. Rushing should be very tough to come by behind that makeshift offensive line.  

 Let's fade Shipley's rushing yards prop in this situation. The Jaguars have been stout against the run this season. Jacksonville is allowing just 3.3 yards per carry, the second-fewest in the league. The defense is also giving up a league-low 47.5 rushing yards per game to opposing running backs. The Jags are stifling every back in their way, and Shipley has to face them with his shaky line.  

 However, Shipley could be productive as a pass-catcher. Jacksonville is allowing the second-most receiving yards (48.3) and receptions (6.75) per game to running backs this year. Teams are getting stuffed in the run game and looking to use their RBs on quick passes. The Eagles should take a similar approach, especially since Jalen Hurts won't have much time to drop back and throw. Plus, Shipley has proven pass-catching chops from his days at Clemson. 

 Meanwhile, the other lead back in this game should be in for a big day. Bhayshul Tuten is averaging 4.6 yards per carry with at least 65 rushing yards in each game. He's gained  73 yards in back-to-back weeks ahead of this matchup. On that note, the Eagles are allowing 106.3 rushing yards per game to opposing RBs, the eighth-highest mark in the league.  

 The Philly defense has also given up 60+ rushing yards to every opposing lead back it's faced this year. In the past two games, the Eagles allowed 84 yards to D'Andre Swift and 80 to Kyren Williams. Tuten can follow suit, especially in a favorable game flow. Jacksonville could be running it a ton in the second half with a lead, considering the touchdown spread.  

 Parlay Odds: +445

<script>
  const KEY = 'bp_display_mode';

  const applyTheme = (mode) => {
    document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', mode);
      try {
        localStorage.setItem(KEY, mode);
      } catch (e) {}
      window._mp_pageview_options = window._mp_pageview_options || {};
      window._mp_pageview_options.display_mode = mode;
  }

  const getPreferredTheme = () => {
    try {
        const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
        const urlMode = params.get('display-mode');
        if (urlMode === 'light' || urlMode === 'dark') return urlMode;

        const darkModeParam = params.get('dark-mode');
        if (darkModeParam === 'true') return 'dark';
        if (darkModeParam === 'false') return 'light';

        const stored = localStorage.getItem(KEY);
        if (stored === 'light' || stored === 'dark') return stored;
      } catch (e) {}

      const prefersDark =
        window.matchMedia &&
        window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
      return prefersDark ? 'dark' : 'light';
  }

  applyTheme(getPreferredTheme());
</script>

<script>
  (function () {
    try {
      const match = document.cookie.match(/(?:^|;\s*)bp_userdata=([^;]*)/);
      let user = null;
      if (match && match[1]) {
        const raw = decodeURIComponent(match[1]).replace(/^"|"$/g, '');
        user = JSON.parse(decodeURIComponent(atob(raw)));
      }
      const level = String((user && user.subscription_level) || '').toLowerCase();
      const premium = level === 'premium' || level === 'goat';
      document.documentElement.setAttribute(
        'data-nav-auth',
        user ? (premium ? 'premium' : 'free') : 'out'
      );

      // Which desktop Upgrade label is coming, because the two are not the same width:
      // the non-trial branch adds a lock icon and a gap before a longer word. Mirrors
      // resolveTrialAudience() — affiliate, then past-trial, else trial — and every input
      // it needs is already in reach here (`bp_affiliate` is its own cookie; the other two
      // are fields on `bp_userdata`). A premium user gets no CTA at all, so no attribute.
      if (!premium) {
        const affiliate =
          /(?:^|;\s*)bp_affiliate=/.test(document.cookie) || Boolean(user && user.affiliate_code);
        const wide = affiliate || Boolean(user && user.has_past_trial);
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-nav-upgrade-label', wide ? 'premium' : 'trial');
      }
    } catch (e) {
      /* leave it unset: every placeholder paints, i.e. the pre-existing behaviour */
    }

    // Separate try/catch, because localStorage throws outright in some privacy modes and a
    // failure here must not cost us the cookie-derived audience above. nav/GetStarted exits
    // on EITHER a signed-in user or this flag, so a logged-out visitor who already finished
    // onboarding gets no CTA and must not be shown a placeholder for one.
    try {
      if (localStorage.getItem('bp_onboarding_completed') === 'true') {
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-nav-onboarded', 'true');
      }
    } catch (e) {
      /* same fail-open: no attribute, placeholder paints */
    }
  })();
</script>

    <div class="article-body-content">
        <p class="article-content__paragraph article-content__paragraph">Let’s look at some of the <span class="article-content__span" style="margin: 0px; padding: 0px;">top<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/systems/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"> premium</a></span><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/systems/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"> betting systems</a> for Week 5. Some of these systems have done incredibly well this season, while others have an outstanding track record over the last few years. Let’s cash in with this week’s best NFL bets.</p>
<ul class="article-content__ul article-content__ul"></ul>
<ul class="article-content__ul article-content__ul"></ul>
<ul class="article-content__ul">
<li class="article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/articles/sports/nfl/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span class="article-content__span">More NFL Betting Advice</span></a></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/picks/prop-bets/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span class="article-content__span">NFL Prop Bet Cheat Sheet</span></a></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/picks/spread-projections/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span class="article-content__span">Expert NFL Game Picks</span></a></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl-betting-guide-strategy-advice/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span class="article-content__span">NFL Betting Strategy</span></a></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/market-ev/nfl/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Best +EV NFL Picks</a></li>
</ul>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><b data-stringify-type="bold"><a class="article-content__anchor c-link" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/appDownload/?tag=bp-articles" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" data-stringify-link="http://bettingpros.com/apps/" data-sk="tooltip_parent">Get instant alerts when a line reaches your target via the BettingPros App >></a></b></p>
<h2 class="article-content__heading"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/picks/prop-bets/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" src="https://www.bettingpros.com/img/PBCS.jpg/0x0.webp" alt="BettingPros Prop Bet Cheat Sheet" width="1920" height="1080" class="article-content__img aligncenter wp-image-300539 size-full" srcset="https://www.bettingpros.com/img/PBCS.jpg/0x0.webp 1920w, https://www.bettingpros.com/img/PBCS-300x169.jpg/300x169.webp 300w, https://www.bettingpros.com/img/PBCS-818x460.jpg/818x460.webp 818w, https://www.bettingpros.com/img/PBCS-768x432.jpg/768x432.webp 768w, https://www.bettingpros.com/img/PBCS-1536x864.jpg/1536x864.webp 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1920px) 100vw, 1920px" /></a></h2>
<h2 class="article-content__heading article-content__heading"><strong>Week 5's Best NFL Bets & Trends Picks</strong></h2>
<p class="article-content__paragraph article-content__paragraph"><em>(Odds courtesy of<span class="article-content__span"> </span><a class="article-content__anchor article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">DraftKings Sportsbook</a>)</em></p>
<h3 class="article-content__subheading typography system-title"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/systems/nfl/chris-olave-receptions-overs-home/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><strong>Chris Olave Receptions Overs (Home)</strong></a></h3>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Chris Olave has hit the over in receptions in seven consecutive home games. His prop line is set at 6.5 this week.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Olave has grabbed at least seven receptions in 70% of his last 10 games and has hit this line in six straight games entering Sunday. He’ll take on a Minnesota Vikings team that has allowed the second-fewest yards on throws behind the sticks. But he’s still had success against these types of defenses.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Let’s ride with the system and take Olave to add at least seven receptions on Sunday.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph article-content__paragraph"><strong>Pick: <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/chris-olave/receptions/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Chris Olave Over 6.5 Receptions</a> <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/george-pickens/receiving-yards/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"></a>(<a class="article-content__anchor article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">+105</a>)</strong></p>
<hr />
<div class="article-content__div article-content__div">
<div class="article-content__div article-content__div">
<div class="article-content__div article-content__div">
<h3 class="article-content__subheading typography system-title"><strong><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/systems/nfl/101-to-120-receptions-unders-20-over-hit-rate-l5/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">-101 to -120 Receptions Unders (≤20% Over Hit Rate L5)</a></strong></h3>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">DK Metcalf has hit the under on his receiving yards prop in six straight home games. He’s got an exciting matchup against the Colts, and just recorded 115 yards against the Browns. But that was a road game.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">All in all, Metcalf has at least 53 receiving yards in just three of his last 10 games and in only 35% of his last 20 games. With Michael Pittman Jr. out, Roman Wilson has been Aaron Rodgers’ favorite target.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Let’s take Metcalf to go under 52.5 receiving yards at home.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph article-content__paragraph"><strong>Pick: <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/dk-metcalf/receiving-yards/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">DK Metcalf Under 52.5 Receiving Yards</a> (<a class="article-content__anchor article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">-114</a>)</strong></p>
<hr />
<div class="article-content__div article-content__div">
<h3 class="article-content__subheading typography system-title"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/systems/nfl/derrick-henry-receptions-unders-away/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><strong>Derrick Henry Receptions Unders (Away)</strong></a></h3>
<div data-v-479e90c1="" class="article-content__div flex system-info">Derrick Henry has at least one reception in two of the first four games this season. However, he’s not known for his catching ability, with at least two catches in just two of his last 10 games, and he has hit this prop in just 30% of his last 20 games.</div>
<div class="article-content__div article-content__div">
<p class="article-content__paragraph">With Lamar Jackson uncertain for Sunday, it’ll be hard to back anyone in the Ravens’ passing game. If Jackson remains out, you’d have to imagine Henry will be mostly used in the run game.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">That’s why, even at <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">-230</a>, backing Henry to finish with fewer than two receptions is a value play. On the road, this has been the case in six consecutive games.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph article-content__paragraph"><strong>Pick: <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/derrick-henry/receptions/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Derrick Henry Under 1.5 Receptions</a> (<a class="article-content__anchor article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">-230</a>)</strong><a class="article-content__anchor article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/articles/nhl-prizepicks-player-predictions-tuesday-panthers-vs-hurricanes/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"></a></p>
</div>

 by Jason Radowitz

Let's look at some of the  top premium  betting systems for Week 5. Some of these systems have done incredibly well this season, while others have an outstanding track record over the last few years. Let's cash in with this week's best NFL bets. 
 
 
 

- More NFL Betting Advice 

- NFL Prop Bet Cheat Sheet 

- Expert NFL Game Picks 

- NFL Betting Strategy 

- Best +EV NFL Picks 
 

 Get instant alerts when a line reaches your target via the BettingPros App 

## 

## Week 5's Best NFL Bets & Trends Picks 

 (Odds courtesy of   DraftKings Sportsbook ) 

### Chris Olave Receptions Overs (Home) 

Chris Olave has hit the over in receptions in seven consecutive home games. His prop line is set at 6.5 this week. 

Olave has grabbed at least seven receptions in 70% of his last 10 games and has hit this line in six straight games entering Sunday. He'll take on a Minnesota Vikings team that has allowed the second-fewest yards on throws behind the sticks. But he's still had success against these types of defenses. 

Let's ride with the system and take Olave to add at least seven receptions on Sunday. 

 Pick: Chris Olave Over 6.5 Receptions ( +105 ) 
 

### -101 to -120 Receptions Unders (≤20% Over Hit Rate L5) 

DK Metcalf has hit the under on his receiving yards prop in six straight home games. He's got an exciting matchup against the Colts, and just recorded 115 yards against the Browns. But that was a road game. 

All in all, Metcalf has at least 53 receiving yards in just three of his last 10 games and in only 35% of his last 20 games. With Michael Pittman Jr. out, Roman Wilson has been Aaron Rodgers' favorite target. 

Let's take Metcalf to go under 52.5 receiving yards at home. 

 Pick: DK Metcalf Under 52.5 Receiving Yards ( -114 ) 
 

### Derrick Henry Receptions Unders (Away) 

Derrick Henry has at least one reception in two of the first four games this season. However, he's not known for his catching ability, with at least two catches in just two of his last 10 games, and he has hit this prop in just 30% of his last 20 games. 

With Lamar Jackson uncertain for Sunday, it'll be hard to back anyone in the Ravens' passing game. If Jackson remains out, you'd have to imagine Henry will be mostly used in the run game. 

That's why, even at -230 , backing Henry to finish with fewer than two receptions is a value play. On the road, this has been the case in six consecutive games. 

 Pick: Derrick Henry Under 1.5 Receptions ( -230 )

<script>

<script>
  (function () {
    try {
      const match = document.cookie.match(/(?:^|;\s*)bp_userdata=([^;]*)/);
      let user = null;
      if (match && match[1]) {
        const raw = decodeURIComponent(match[1]).replace(/^"|"$/g, '');
        user = JSON.parse(decodeURIComponent(atob(raw)));
      }
      const level = String((user && user.subscription_level) || '').toLowerCase();
      const premium = level === 'premium' || level === 'goat';
      document.documentElement.setAttribute(
        'data-nav-auth',
        user ? (premium ? 'premium' : 'free') : 'out'
      );

      // Which desktop Upgrade label is coming, because the two are not the same width:
      // the non-trial branch adds a lock icon and a gap before a longer word. Mirrors
      // resolveTrialAudience() — affiliate, then past-trial, else trial — and every input
      // it needs is already in reach here (`bp_affiliate` is its own cookie; the other two
      // are fields on `bp_userdata`). A premium user gets no CTA at all, so no attribute.
      if (!premium) {
        const affiliate =
          /(?:^|;\s*)bp_affiliate=/.test(document.cookie) || Boolean(user && user.affiliate_code);
        const wide = affiliate || Boolean(user && user.has_past_trial);
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-nav-upgrade-label', wide ? 'premium' : 'trial');
      }
    } catch (e) {
      /* leave it unset: every placeholder paints, i.e. the pre-existing behaviour */
    }

    // Separate try/catch, because localStorage throws outright in some privacy modes and a
    // failure here must not cost us the cookie-derived audience above. nav/GetStarted exits
    // on EITHER a signed-in user or this flag, so a logged-out visitor who already finished
    // onboarding gets no CTA and must not be shown a placeholder for one.
    try {
      if (localStorage.getItem('bp_onboarding_completed') === 'true') {
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-nav-onboarded', 'true');
      }
    } catch (e) {
      /* same fail-open: no attribute, placeholder paints */
    }
  })();
</script>

        <p class="article-content__paragraph article-content__paragraph article-content__paragraph">The NFL season rolls on with an exciting Week 5 slate on tap. It’s time to lock in our<span class="article-content__span article-content__span"> </span><a class="article-content__anchor article-content__anchor article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/parlay-wizard/nfl/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">NFL Week 5 anytime TD scorer & win parlays</a>. The strategy behind these picks is simple. We’re parlaying a team’s Moneyline to win and a player’s anytime touchdown scorer odds. Pairing the picks can improve our payouts and give us a fun alternative way to get action on the week’s games.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph article-content__paragraph article-content__paragraph">Without further ado, let’s dive into my favorite anytime TD and win parlays for Week 5.</p>
<ul class="article-content__ul article-content__ul">
<li class="article-content__list-item article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/articles/sports/nfl/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span class="article-content__span article-content__span">More NFL Betting Advice</span></a></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/picks/prop-bets/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span class="article-content__span article-content__span">NFL Prop Bet Cheat Sheet</span></a></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/picks/spread-projections/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span class="article-content__span article-content__span">Expert NFL Game Picks</span></a></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl-betting-guide-strategy-advice/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span class="article-content__span article-content__span">NFL Betting Strategy</span></a></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/market-ev/nfl/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Best +EV NFL Picks</a></li>
</ul>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><b data-stringify-type="bold"><a class="article-content__anchor c-link" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/appDownload/?tag=bp-articles" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" data-stringify-link="http://bettingpros.com/apps/" data-sk="tooltip_parent">Get instant alerts when a line reaches your target via the BettingPros App >></a></b></p>

<h2 class="article-content__heading article-content__heading article-content__heading article-content__heading"><strong><span class="article-content__span article-content__span article-content__span article-content__span" data-preserver-spaces="true">NFL Week 5 Anytime TD Scorer & Win Parlays</span></strong></h2>
<p class="article-content__paragraph article-content__paragraph article-content__paragraph article-content__paragraph"><i>(Odds courtesy of<span class="article-content__span article-content__span article-content__span"> </span><a class="article-content__anchor article-content__anchor article-content__anchor article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">DraftKings Sportsbook</a>)</i></p>
<h3 class="article-content__subheading"><b>Detroit Lions at Arizona Cardinals </b><b></b></h3>
<ul class="article-content__ul">
<li class="article-content__list-item"><b>Leg 1: <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/matchups/arizona-cardinals-vs-detroit-lions/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Lions Moneyline</a> (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">-258</a>)</b></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item"><b>Leg 2: <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/amonra-stbrown/receiving-yards/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Amon-Ra St. Brown Anytime Touchdown Scorer</a> (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">-140</a>)</b></li>
</ul>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">Let's start off our touchdown & win parlays with Arizona hosting Detroit. The 2-2 Lions are looking to rebound after losing to the Panthers last Sunday night. They're favored on the road against the 1-3 Cardinals, who have lost three straight. </span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">Detroit has been a trustworthy team to back after losing under head coach Dan Campbell. Over the past four seasons, the Lions are 14-2 following a loss. Campbell simply knows how to get his squad to respond in these spots. It's also a big opportunity for Detroit to head into next week's bye with a winning record. </span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">Meanwhile, Arizona is in a tailspin after its Week 1 win. The Cardinals are allowing 34.3 points per game in their current three-game losing streak. Their shaky defense now faces a high-powered Detroit attack that's averaging 29.8 points per game (PPG) this season. The Lions' defense hasn't been any better, but Jared Goff and the offense should pace them to victory. </span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">As the Lions put up points, Amon-Ra St. Brown is a good pick to score. Detroit's star wideout has five touchdowns through four games. He was held out of the end zone last week, but is in a prime spot to get back there. The Cardinals have allowed a league-high eight touchdowns to opposing wide receivers this season. </span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">St. Brown also has a whopping 46 red-zone targets over the first four games. That includes at least 11 targets in three of the four weeks. Goff is looking his way plenty near the end zone. Combine that with Arizona’s tendency to allow touchdowns to wideouts, and St. Brown should help cash this parlay.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><b>Parlay Odds: <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">+126</a></b></p>
<hr />
<h3 class="article-content__subheading"><b>Indianapolis Colts at Pittsburgh Steelers </b><b></b></h3>
<ul class="article-content__ul">
<li class="article-content__list-item"><b>Leg 1: <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/matchups/indianapolis-colts-vs-pittsburgh-steelers/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Steelers Moneyline</a> (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">-148</a>)</b></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item"><b>Leg 2: <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/roman-wilson-wr/receiving-yards/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Roman Wilson Anytime Touchdown Scorer</a> (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">+285</a>)</b></li>
</ul>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">Let's go with some longer odds for our second parlay. The 2-2 Steelers return home after losing at Cleveland last week. They're 3-point favorites against the 2-2 Colts, who are fresh off beating the Commanders in London. Take Pittsburgh to bounce back and beat Indianapolis. </span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">The Colts have been dealt a tough hand, having to play on the road right after a trip to London. It's always a tough spot for NFL teams without a bye week in between games. Plus, Indianapolis is still very unproven this season. Its two wins have come against the 0-4 Texans and a Washington squad that was down to its third-string quarterback last week. </span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">Before that, the Indianapolis defense allowed 41 and 33 points in its first two losses to Baltimore and Kansas City, respectively. The Colts' defensive struggles could return on the road against Aaron Rodgers and Co. this week, especially against the pass. Meanwhile, Pittsburgh's offense has woken up lately. The Steelers should have success through the air to control the game and come out with a win. </span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">On that note, bank on Roman Wilson finding the end zone. The Pittsburgh wideout has scored in back-to-back games coming into this weekend. He can make it three straight, as the Colts have allowed four touchdowns to opposing wide receivers so far. Indianapolis is also allowing the seventh-most receiving yards per game to wide receivers. </span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">Plus, Wilson's 24 red-zone targets this year are second on the team behind DK Metcalf. The latter might be the safer bet to score, but Wilson offers juicier odds. He's seen a consistent six red-zone targets in all four games thus far. </span></p>

<hr />

 by Dan Servodidio

The NFL season rolls on with an exciting Week 5 slate on tap. It's time to lock in our   NFL Week 5 anytime TD scorer & win parlays . The strategy behind these picks is simple. We're parlaying a team's Moneyline to win and a player's anytime touchdown scorer odds. Pairing the picks can improve our payouts and give us a fun alternative way to get action on the week's games. 

Without further ado, let's dive into my favorite anytime TD and win parlays for Week 5. 
 

- More NFL Betting Advice 

- NFL Prop Bet Cheat Sheet 

- Expert NFL Game Picks 

- NFL Betting Strategy 

- Best +EV NFL Picks 
 

 Get instant alerts when a line reaches your target via the BettingPros App 

## 

## NFL Week 5 Anytime TD Scorer & Win Parlays 

 (Odds courtesy of   DraftKings Sportsbook ) 

### Detroit Lions at Arizona Cardinals  

 

- Leg 1: Lions Moneyline ( -258 ) 

- Leg 2: Amon-Ra St. Brown Anytime Touchdown Scorer ( -140 ) 
 

 Let's start off our touchdown & win parlays with Arizona hosting Detroit. The 2-2 Lions are looking to rebound after losing to the Panthers last Sunday night. They're favored on the road against the 1-3 Cardinals, who have lost three straight.  

 Detroit has been a trustworthy team to back after losing under head coach Dan Campbell. Over the past four seasons, the Lions are 14-2 following a loss. Campbell simply knows how to get his squad to respond in these spots. It's also a big opportunity for Detroit to head into next week's bye with a winning record.  

 Meanwhile, Arizona is in a tailspin after its Week 1 win. The Cardinals are allowing 34.3 points per game in their current three-game losing streak. Their shaky defense now faces a high-powered Detroit attack that's averaging 29.8 points per game (PPG) this season. The Lions' defense hasn't been any better, but Jared Goff and the offense should pace them to victory.  

 As the Lions put up points, Amon-Ra St. Brown is a good pick to score. Detroit's star wideout has five touchdowns through four games. He was held out of the end zone last week, but is in a prime spot to get back there. The Cardinals have allowed a league-high eight touchdowns to opposing wide receivers this season.  

St. Brown also has a whopping 46 red-zone targets over the first four games. That includes at least 11 targets in three of the four weeks. Goff is looking his way plenty near the end zone. Combine that with Arizona's tendency to allow touchdowns to wideouts, and St. Brown should help cash this parlay. 

 Parlay Odds: +126 
 

### Indianapolis Colts at Pittsburgh Steelers  

 

- Leg 1: Steelers Moneyline ( -148 ) 

- Leg 2: Roman Wilson Anytime Touchdown Scorer ( +285 ) 
 

 Let's go with some longer odds for our second parlay. The 2-2 Steelers return home after losing at Cleveland last week. They're 3-point favorites against the 2-2 Colts, who are fresh off beating the Commanders in London. Take Pittsburgh to bounce back and beat Indianapolis.  

 The Colts have been dealt a tough hand, having to play on the road right after a trip to London. It's always a tough spot for NFL teams without a bye week in between games. Plus, Indianapolis is still very unproven this season. Its two wins have come against the 0-4 Texans and a Washington squad that was down to its third-string quarterback last week.  

 Before that, the Indianapolis defense allowed 41 and 33 points in its first two losses to Baltimore and Kansas City, respectively. The Colts' defensive struggles could return on the road against Aaron Rodgers and Co. this week, especially against the pass. Meanwhile, Pittsburgh's offense has woken up lately. The Steelers should have success through the air to control the game and come out with a win.  

 On that note, bank on Roman Wilson finding the end zone. The Pittsburgh wideout has scored in back-to-back games coming into this weekend. He can make it three straight, as the Colts have allowed four touchdowns to opposing wide receivers so far. Indianapolis is also allowing the seventh-most receiving yards per game to wide receivers.  

 Plus, Wilson's 24 red-zone targets this year are second on the team behind DK Metcalf. The latter might be the safer bet to score, but Wilson offers juicier odds. He's seen a consistent six red-zone targets in all four games thus far.  

 Parlay Odds: +465

  (function () {
    try {
      const match = document.cookie.match(/(?:^|;\s*)bp_userdata=([^;]*)/);
      let user = null;
      if (match && match[1]) {
        const raw = decodeURIComponent(match[1]).replace(/^"|"$/g, '');
        user = JSON.parse(decodeURIComponent(atob(raw)));
      }
      const level = String((user && user.subscription_level) || '').toLowerCase();
      const premium = level === 'premium' || level === 'goat';
      document.documentElement.setAttribute(
        'data-nav-auth',
        user ? (premium ? 'premium' : 'free') : 'out'
      );

      // Which desktop Upgrade label is coming, because the two are not the same width:
      // the non-trial branch adds a lock icon and a gap before a longer word. Mirrors
      // resolveTrialAudience() — affiliate, then past-trial, else trial — and every input
      // it needs is already in reach here (`bp_affiliate` is its own cookie; the other two
      // are fields on `bp_userdata`). A premium user gets no CTA at all, so no attribute.
      if (!premium) {
        const affiliate =
          /(?:^|;\s*)bp_affiliate=/.test(document.cookie) || Boolean(user && user.affiliate_code);
        const wide = affiliate || Boolean(user && user.has_past_trial);
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-nav-upgrade-label', wide ? 'premium' : 'trial');
      }
    } catch (e) {
      /* leave it unset: every placeholder paints, i.e. the pre-existing behaviour */
    }

    // Separate try/catch, because localStorage throws outright in some privacy modes and a
    // failure here must not cost us the cookie-derived audience above. nav/GetStarted exits
    // on EITHER a signed-in user or this flag, so a logged-out visitor who already finished
    // onboarding gets no CTA and must not be shown a placeholder for one.
    try {
      if (localStorage.getItem('bp_onboarding_completed') === 'true') {
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-nav-onboarded', 'true');
      }
    } catch (e) {
      /* same fail-open: no attribute, placeholder paints */
    }
  })();

        <p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">The Lions versus Cardinals game has the highest projected total of the week. Below, I explain why I expect the Lions to fully capitalize on the Cardinals' struggling defense after a disappointing Week 4 result. Then I highlight why it’s worth taking a shot on Omarion Hampton and Cam Ward in favorable matchups. </span><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">Here are the best <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/picks/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">longshot NFL Week 5 picks</a>. </span></p>
<ul class="article-content__ul">
<li class="article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/articles/sports/nfl/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span class="article-content__span">More NFL Betting Advice</span></a></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/picks/prop-bets/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span class="article-content__span">NFL Prop Bet Cheat Sheet</span></a></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/picks/spread-projections/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span class="article-content__span">Expert NFL Game Picks</span></a></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl-betting-guide-strategy-advice/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span class="article-content__span">NFL Betting Strategy</span></a></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/market-ev/nfl/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Best +EV NFL Picks</a></li>
</ul>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><b data-stringify-type="bold"><a class="article-content__anchor c-link" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/appDownload/?tag=bp-articles" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" data-stringify-link="http://bettingpros.com/apps/" data-sk="tooltip_parent">Get instant alerts when a line reaches your target via the BettingPros App >></a></b></p>
<h2 class="article-content__heading"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/picks/prop-bets/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" src="https://www.bettingpros.com/img/PBCS.jpg/0x0.webp" alt="BettingPros Prop Bet Cheat Shhet" width="1920" height="1080" class="article-content__img aligncenter wp-image-300539 size-full" srcset="https://www.bettingpros.com/img/PBCS.jpg/0x0.webp 1920w, https://www.bettingpros.com/img/PBCS-300x169.jpg/300x169.webp 300w, https://www.bettingpros.com/img/PBCS-818x460.jpg/818x460.webp 818w, https://www.bettingpros.com/img/PBCS-768x432.jpg/768x432.webp 768w, https://www.bettingpros.com/img/PBCS-1536x864.jpg/1536x864.webp 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1920px) 100vw, 1920px" /></a></h2>
<h2 class="article-content__heading"><strong>NFL Week 5 Picks: Sleepers & Longshot Bets </strong></h2>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><em>(Odds Courtesy of<span class="article-content__span"> </span><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">DraftKings Sportsbook</a>)</em></p>
<h3 class="article-content__subheading"><b><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/matchups/arizona-cardinals-vs-detroit-lions/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Lions Over 40.5 Points</a> (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">+500</a>)</b></h3>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">There has been such an emphasis on how bad the Lions' defense has been that the offense's excellent play is being overlooked. The Lions have scored at least 26 points in all four games, giving them the fifth-highest-scoring offense in the league thus far. Jared Goff is off to an insane start with 1,214 yards, 9 touchdowns and 0 interceptions, and Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown have combined for nine touchdowns.</span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">This week, the Lions face a defense that is almost as bad as their own. The Cardinals are allowing 29.3 points per game, the fourth-most in the NFL. The defense ranks in the bottom 10 in total yards allowed and 30th in yards per play allowed (6.1).</span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">I fully expect the Lions to score at will in this game, and I don't expect them to stop at any point, because their defense is so untrustworthy. After all, the Lions blew a 21-point lead in Week 1 and a 14-point lead in Week 3. The Cardinals will score plenty in this game, but I wouldn't be surprised if the Lions score a touchdown on nearly every drive.</span></p>
<hr />
<h3 class="article-content__subheading"><b><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/omarion-hampton/rushing-yards/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Omarion Hampton 70+ Rushing Yards</a> (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">+479</a>)</b></h3>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">The Chargers' offense has been abysmal this season. They're averaging just 16.8 points and 306.8 total yards per game. However, the rushing attack actually ranks ninth-best in the league. </span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">Omarion Hampton has rushed for at least 43 yards in all four games, despite the Chargers losing every game by at least seven points. He's averaging 4.0 yards per carry, and he managed 94 yards against the Raiders.</span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">The Broncos are allowing 142.8 rushing yards per game, which is the fourth-most in the NFL. They're also giving up 4.8 yards per carry, which is tied for the fifth-worst mark in the league. Hampton has received more than 12 carries just twice this season, but with the Broncos barely favored in a low-scoring game, I expect him to get enough touches to properly exploit this weak run defense.</span></p>
<hr />
<h3 class="article-content__subheading"><b><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/cam-ward/passing-yards/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Cam Ward 260+ Passing Yards</a> (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">+505</a>)</b></h3>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">In two games against the Texans last season, Cam Ward never threw for more than 194 yards. In his first game against the team, he completed just 10 of his 26 passes for 108 yards. However, that pass defense finished as the league's sixth-best last season. This year's pass defense currently ranks fifth-worst.</span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">The Texans are allowing an average of 260 passing yards per game. While Ward is yet to top 222 yards in a game this season, he is completing 63% of his passes. That's up from 59.8% last season.</span></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><span class="article-content__span" style="font-weight: 400;">The Texans are favored by 7.5 points, so I expect Ward to be throwing for the majority of this game. And while his career-high is just 265 yards, Ward threw for at least 150 yards in five games last season. And he started to play significantly better in Week 5.</span></p>
<hr />

 by Phil Wood

 by Phil Wood

 The Lions versus Cardinals game has the highest projected total of the week. Below, I explain why I expect the Lions to fully capitalize on the Cardinals' struggling defense after a disappointing Week 4 result. Then I highlight why it's worth taking a shot on Omarion Hampton and Cam Ward in favorable matchups. Here are the best longshot NFL Week 5 picks .  
 

- More NFL Betting Advice

 Get instant alerts when a line reaches your target via the BettingPros App 

## 

## NFL Week 5 Picks: Sleepers & Longshot Bets  

 (Odds Courtesy of   DraftKings Sportsbook ) 

### Lions Over 40.5 Points ( +500 ) 

 There has been such an emphasis on how bad the Lions' defense has been that the offense's excellent play is being overlooked. The Lions have scored at least 26 points in all four games, giving them the fifth-highest-scoring offense in the league thus far. Jared Goff is off to an insane start with 1,214 yards, 9 touchdowns and 0 interceptions, and Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown have combined for nine touchdowns. 

 This week, the Lions face a defense that is almost as bad as their own. The Cardinals are allowing 29.3 points per game, the fourth-most in the NFL. The defense ranks in the bottom 10 in total yards allowed and 30th in yards per play allowed (6.1). 

 I fully expect the Lions to score at will in this game, and I don't expect them to stop at any point, because their defense is so untrustworthy. After all, the Lions blew a 21-point lead in Week 1 and a 14-point lead in Week 3. The Cardinals will score plenty in this game, but I wouldn't be surprised if the Lions score a touchdown on nearly every drive. 
 

### Omarion Hampton 70+ Rushing Yards ( +479 ) 

 The Chargers' offense has been abysmal this season. They're averaging just 16.8 points and 306.8 total yards per game. However, the rushing attack actually ranks ninth-best in the league.  

 Omarion Hampton has rushed for at least 43 yards in all four games, despite the Chargers losing every game by at least seven points. He's averaging 4.0 yards per carry, and he managed 94 yards against the Raiders. 

 The Broncos are allowing 142.8 rushing yards per game, which is the fourth-most in the NFL. They're also giving up 4.8 yards per carry, which is tied for the fifth-worst mark in the league. Hampton has received more than 12 carries just twice this season, but with the Broncos barely favored in a low-scoring game, I expect him to get enough touches to properly exploit this weak run defense. 
 

### Cam Ward 260+ Passing Yards ( +505 ) 

 In two games against the Texans last season, Cam Ward never threw for more than 194 yards. In his first game against the team, he completed just 10 of his 26 passes for 108 yards. However, that pass defense finished as the league's sixth-best last season. This year's pass defense currently ranks fifth-worst. 

 The Texans are allowing an average of 260 passing yards per game. While Ward is yet to top 222 yards in a game this season, he is completing 63% of his passes. That's up from 59.8% last season. 

 The Texans are favored by 7.5 points, so I expect Ward to be throwing for the majority of this game. And while his career-high is just 265 yards, Ward threw for at least 150 yards in five games last season. And he started to play significantly better in Week 5.

<script>
  (function () {
    try {
      const match = document.cookie.match(/(?:^|;\s*)bp_userdata=([^;]*)/);
      let user = null;
      if (match && match[1]) {
        const raw = decodeURIComponent(match[1]).replace(/^"|"$/g, '');
        user = JSON.parse(decodeURIComponent(atob(raw)));
      }
      const level = String((user && user.subscription_level) || '').toLowerCase();
      const premium = level === 'premium' || level === 'goat';
      document.documentElement.setAttribute(
        'data-nav-auth',
        user ? (premium ? 'premium' : 'free') : 'out'
      );

      // Which desktop Upgrade label is coming, because the two are not the same width:
      // the non-trial branch adds a lock icon and a gap before a longer word. Mirrors
      // resolveTrialAudience() — affiliate, then past-trial, else trial — and every input
      // it needs is already in reach here (`bp_affiliate` is its own cookie; the other two
      // are fields on `bp_userdata`). A premium user gets no CTA at all, so no attribute.
      if (!premium) {
        const affiliate =
          /(?:^|;\s*)bp_affiliate=/.test(document.cookie) || Boolean(user && user.affiliate_code);
        const wide = affiliate || Boolean(user && user.has_past_trial);
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-nav-upgrade-label', wide ? 'premium' : 'trial');
      }
    } catch (e) {
      /* leave it unset: every placeholder paints, i.e. the pre-existing behaviour */
    }

    // Separate try/catch, because localStorage throws outright in some privacy modes and a
    // failure here must not cost us the cookie-derived audience above. nav/GetStarted exits
    // on EITHER a signed-in user or this flag, so a logged-out visitor who already finished
    // onboarding gets no CTA and must not be shown a placeholder for one.
    try {
      if (localStorage.getItem('bp_onboarding_completed') === 'true') {
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-nav-onboarded', 'true');
      }
    } catch (e) {
      /* same fail-open: no attribute, placeholder paints */
    }
  })();
</script>

<h3 class="article-content__subheading"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/ashton-jeanty/receptions/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><strong>Ashton Jeanty More Than 3.5 Receptions</strong></a></h3>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Ashton Jeanty is showing a complete skill set this season. He has 24 targets, 19 receptions and 165 receiving yards through four games with Kirk Cousins under center. Teams have to focus on Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer in this offense, which typically relies on linebackers and safeties. Jeanty is benefiting as a receiver.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Jeanty has not scored a rushing touchdown, while he has two through the air. The end zone is tough to find, but targets are not. The Patriots are allowing 4.3 receptions per game to running backs. Jeanty is coming off a game with eight targets, so he should have plenty of opportunities to find four receptions this week.</p>
<hr />
<h3 class="article-content__subheading"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/chase-brown/rushing-attempts/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><strong>Chase Brown More Than 16.5 Rush Attempts</strong></a></h3>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The Bengals are banged up this week, but luckily, they play the Dolphins. The Dolphins are averaging a league-low 11.5 points per game. The Bengals are favored by 6.5 points, and Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor/neck) are both questionable. Chase will have to clear concussion protocol, and Higgins was not at practice on Thursday.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The wrinkle is that the Bengals have a bye week after this game. They could easily use this game as an extra week of recovery for their star receivers. Brown would see an increase in usage if both miss. Even if they both play, the Bengals should lean on Brown against this defense.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The Dolphins' offense cannot keep them in this game, and the Bengals should have a positive game script for Brown rushing attempts. He has achieved this total only once this season, in a 20-6 victory over the Texans. This game could play out similarly, and Brown can hit this total for the second time this season.</p>

<li class="article-content__list-item">2.80 yards per route run</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">24.7% first-read share</li>
</ul>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The matchup is not perfect this week, but it should be a competitive game throughout.</p>

## Best NFL Week 5 PrizePicks Player Predictions 

### Ashton Jeanty More Than 3.5 Receptions 

Ashton Jeanty is showing a complete skill set this season. He has 24 targets, 19 receptions and 165 receiving yards through four games with Kirk Cousins under center. Teams have to focus on Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer in this offense, which typically relies on linebackers and safeties. Jeanty is benefiting as a receiver. 

Jeanty has not scored a rushing touchdown, while he has two through the air. The end zone is tough to find, but targets are not. The Patriots are allowing 4.3 receptions per game to running backs. Jeanty is coming off a game with eight targets, so he should have plenty of opportunities to find four receptions this week. 
 

### Chase Brown More Than 16.5 Rush Attempts 

The Bengals are banged up this week, but luckily, they play the Dolphins. The Dolphins are averaging a league-low 11.5 points per game. The Bengals are favored by 6.5 points, and Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor/neck) are both questionable. Chase will have to clear concussion protocol, and Higgins was not at practice on Thursday. 

The wrinkle is that the Bengals have a bye week after this game. They could easily use this game as an extra week of recovery for their star receivers. Brown would see an increase in usage if both miss. Even if they both play, the Bengals should lean on Brown against this defense. 

The Dolphins' offense cannot keep them in this game, and the Bengals should have a positive game script for Brown rushing attempts. He has achieved this total only once this season, in a 20-6 victory over the Texans. This game could play out similarly, and Brown can hit this total for the second time this season. 
 

### Mike Evans More Than 47.5 Receiving Yards 

Mike Evans played through a rib injury last week and caught five passes, grimacing after each. He is still elite at 33, and his stats prove it: 
 

- 60.8% route share 

- 21.2% target share 

- 2.80 yards per route run 

- 24.7% first-read share 
 

The matchup is not perfect this week, but it should be a competitive game throughout. 

Evans has always shown up in big games. He is still separating at a high rate, and Brock Purdy is playing phenomenal football. He is finding Evans when he is on the field. Evans has exceeded this total in three out of four games and should be involved a lot in this matchup.

<script>
  const KEY = 'bp_display_mode';

  const applyTheme = (mode) => {
    document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', mode);

      } catch (e) {}
      window._mp_pageview_options = window._mp_pageview_options || {};

  }

  const getPreferredTheme = () => {
    try {
        const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
        const urlMode = params.get('display-mode');
        if (urlMode === 'light' || urlMode === 'dark') return urlMode;

        const darkModeParam = params.get('dark-mode');
        if (darkModeParam === 'true') return 'dark';
        if (darkModeParam === 'false') return 'light';

        const stored = localStorage.getItem(KEY);
        if (stored === 'light' || stored === 'dark') return stored;
      } catch (e) {}

      const prefersDark =
        window.matchMedia &&
        window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
      return prefersDark ? 'dark' : 'light';
  }

  applyTheme(getPreferredTheme());
</script>

<script>
  (function () {
    try {
      const match = document.cookie.match(/(?:^|;\s*)bp_userdata=([^;]*)/);
      let user = null;
      if (match && match[1]) {
        const raw = decodeURIComponent(match[1]).replace(/^"|"$/g, '');
        user = JSON.parse(decodeURIComponent(atob(raw)));
      }
      const level = String((user && user.subscription_level) || '').toLowerCase();
      const premium = level === 'premium' || level === 'goat';
      document.documentElement.setAttribute(
        'data-nav-auth',
        user ? (premium ? 'premium' : 'free') : 'out'
      );

      // Which desktop Upgrade label is coming, because the two are not the same width:
      // the non-trial branch adds a lock icon and a gap before a longer word. Mirrors
      // resolveTrialAudience() — affiliate, then past-trial, else trial — and every input
      // it needs is already in reach here (`bp_affiliate` is its own cookie; the other two
      // are fields on `bp_userdata`). A premium user gets no CTA at all, so no attribute.
      if (!premium) {
        const affiliate =
          /(?:^|;\s*)bp_affiliate=/.test(document.cookie) || Boolean(user && user.affiliate_code);
        const wide = affiliate || Boolean(user && user.has_past_trial);
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-nav-upgrade-label', wide ? 'premium' : 'trial');
      }
    } catch (e) {
      /* leave it unset: every placeholder paints, i.e. the pre-existing behaviour */
    }

    // Separate try/catch, because localStorage throws outright in some privacy modes and a
    // failure here must not cost us the cookie-derived audience above. nav/GetStarted exits
    // on EITHER a signed-in user or this flag, so a logged-out visitor who already finished
    // onboarding gets no CTA and must not be shown a placeholder for one.
    try {
      if (localStorage.getItem('bp_onboarding_completed') === 'true') {
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-nav-onboarded', 'true');
      }
    } catch (e) {
      /* same fail-open: no attribute, placeholder paints */
    }
  })();
</script>
