    <div class="article-body-content">
        <p class="article-content__paragraph">Underdogs had another solid week, with five winning outright on Sunday and three more covering against the spread (ATS). That brings underdogs to 25-39 straight up (SU) and 34-23-1 ATS so far. Betting on underdogs has been a good idea this season. How about this week? After reviewing the games scheduled for Sunday, the following are my top underdog <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/picks/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">NFL Week 5 picks</a>.</p>
<ul class="article-content__ul">
<li class="article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/articles/sports/nfl/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span class="article-content__span">More NFL Betting Advice</span></a></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/picks/prop-bets/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span class="article-content__span">NFL Prop Bet Cheat Sheet</span></a></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/picks/spread-projections/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span class="article-content__span">Expert NFL Game Picks</span></a></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl-betting-guide-strategy-advice/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><span class="article-content__span">NFL Betting Strategy</span></a></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/market-ev/nfl/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Best +EV NFL Picks</a></li>
</ul>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/appDownload/?tag=bp-articles" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" data-stringify-link="http://bettingpros.com/apps/" data-sk="tooltip_parent">Get instant alerts when a line reaches your target via the BettingPros App >></a></strong></p>
<h2 class="article-content__heading"><a class="article-content__anchor article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/picks/prizepicks/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" src="https://www.bettingpros.com/img/prizepicks_optimizer.jpg/0x0.webp" alt="The PrizePicks & Underdog DFS Optimizers at BettingPros help you build the best pickem slips, with a focus on finding value on the board." width="1470" height="650" class="article-content__img article-content__img aligncenter wp-image-332112 size-full" srcset="https://www.bettingpros.com/img/prizepicks_optimizer.jpg/0x0.webp 1470w, https://www.bettingpros.com/img/prizepicks_optimizer-300x133.jpg/300x133.webp 300w, https://www.bettingpros.com/img/prizepicks_optimizer-818x362.jpg/818x362.webp 818w, https://www.bettingpros.com/img/prizepicks_optimizer-768x340.jpg/768x340.webp 768w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1470px) 100vw, 1470px" /></a></h2>
<h2 class="article-content__heading"><strong>NFL Week 5 Picks & Predictions: Underdog Bets</strong></h2>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><em>(Odds courtesy of <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">DraftKings Sportsbook</a>)</em></p>
<h3 class="article-content__subheading"><strong>Cleveland Browns vs. New York Jets</strong></h3>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">I hate to even think this, let alone type it, but the Browns are getting underestimated in this game (or maybe it's the Jets being <em>overestimated</em>). Statistically, the Jets should have an edge on defense, but with how Deshaun Watson has played the last few weeks, that may not be the case.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Yes, the Browns offense still has its faults. But Watson has improved week after week and made some incredible plays in clutch moments for the 3-1 Cleveland Browns (first in the AFC North). The Jets have played solid defense, but their offense has struggled, averaging 286 yards and 19 points per game. However, the Browns haven't done much better (292.5 yards and 20.3 points per game).</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">If you want to be cautious, take the points (+2.5), as this game will likely be close. But with how Watson and the Browns have been playing, I expect Cleveland to come out on top against this lackluster Jets team.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Pick: Browns Moneyline (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">+114</a>)</strong></p>
<hr />
<h3 class="article-content__subheading"><strong>San Francisco 49ers vs. Seattle Seahawks</strong></h3>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The Seattle defense is incredible, but the 49ers have so many weapons on offense, and Brock Purdy has been playing lights out. With the Seahawks still struggling to establish the run, the 49ers’ defense may have a slight edge against Sam Darnold and Seattle's pass-dependent offense.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">This will be a great, low-scoring game (much like last year's regular-season matchups) that either team could win outright. But since these are two really good teams, I'd suggest taking the 49ers and the points (+3) over the San Francisco Moneyline (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">+136</a>).</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Pick: 49ers +3 (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">-110</a>)</strong></p>
<hr />
<h3 class="article-content__subheading"><strong>Las Vegas Raiders vs. New England Patriots</strong></h3>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">I can't shake the feeling this line is inflated for the Patriots because Drake Maye and the offense had such a good game against a lackluster Bills defense last week. Maybe they’re on track now and just needed one game to shake off the doldrums that had controlled them for the first three weeks. Or maybe they took advantage of Buffalo's questionable defense and an inconsistent day for Josh Allen and the Bills’ offense.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Kirk Cousins and the Raiders have been one of the season’s more pleasant surprises so far. Despite a late turnover that gave Kansas City an 11-point lead with three minutes to go, they nearly got into field goal range and had a chance to send the game to overtime. This is not the same old Raiders. It's a team with talent that is well-coached and not folding under pressure.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">They absolutely have a chance to win this one outright, but at the least, they'll stay within three points.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Picks: Raiders +3.5 (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">-110</a>) & Browns Moneyline (<a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://dksb.sng.link/As9kz/zdg8?_dl=https%3A%2F%2Fsportsbook.draftkings.com%2Fgateway%3Fs%3D801206430%26wpcid%3D255224%26wpsrc%3D1756%26wpcn%3DNFLPlayoffs2023%26wpscn%3DBet5Get200%26wpcrn%3DFP1%26wpscid%3Dxx%26wpcrid%3Dxx&pcid=255224" target="_blank" rel="noopener">+164</a>)</strong></p>
<hr />
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/appDownload/?tag=bp-articles" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" src="https://www.bettingpros.com/img/bettingpros_app_launch_1470650.png/0x0.webp" alt="BettingPros App 3.0" width="1470" height="650" class="article-content__img aligncenter wp-image-300808 size-full" srcset="https://www.bettingpros.com/img/bettingpros_app_launch_1470650.png/0x0.webp 1470w, https://www.bettingpros.com/img/bettingpros_app_launch_1470650-300x133.png/300x133.webp 300w, https://www.bettingpros.com/img/bettingpros_app_launch_1470650-818x362.png/818x362.webp 818w, https://www.bettingpros.com/img/bettingpros_app_launch_1470650-768x340.png/768x340.webp 768w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1470px) 100vw, 1470px" /></a></p>

# NFL Week 5 Picks & Predictions: Underdog Bets (2026)

 

 

 
 by Travis Pulver 
 | 
 Oct 10, 2026 
 
 
 

 

 
 by Travis Pulver 
 | 
 Oct 10, 2026 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 

 
Underdogs had another solid week, with five winning outright on Sunday and three more covering against the spread (ATS). That brings underdogs to 25-39 straight up (SU) and 34-23-1 ATS so far. Betting on underdogs has been a good idea this season. How about this week? After reviewing the games scheduled for Sunday, the following are my top underdog NFL Week 5 picks . 
 

- More NFL Betting Advice 

- NFL Prop Bet Cheat Sheet 

- Expert NFL Game Picks 

- NFL Betting Strategy 

- Best +EV NFL Picks 
 

 Get instant alerts when a line reaches your target via the BettingPros App 

## 

## NFL Week 5 Picks & Predictions: Underdog Bets 

 (Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook ) 

### Cleveland Browns vs. New York Jets 

I hate to even think this, let alone type it, but the Browns are getting underestimated in this game (or maybe it's the Jets being overestimated ). Statistically, the Jets should have an edge on defense, but with how Deshaun Watson has played the last few weeks, that may not be the case. 

Yes, the Browns offense still has its faults. But Watson has improved week after week and made some incredible plays in clutch moments for the 3-1 Cleveland Browns (first in the AFC North). The Jets have played solid defense, but their offense has struggled, averaging 286 yards and 19 points per game. However, the Browns haven't done much better (292.5 yards and 20.3 points per game). 

If you want to be cautious, take the points (+2.5), as this game will likely be close. But with how Watson and the Browns have been playing, I expect Cleveland to come out on top against this lackluster Jets team. 

 Pick: Browns Moneyline ( +114 ) 
 

### San Francisco 49ers vs. Seattle Seahawks 

The Seattle defense is incredible, but the 49ers have so many weapons on offense, and Brock Purdy has been playing lights out. With the Seahawks still struggling to establish the run, the 49ers' defense may have a slight edge against Sam Darnold and Seattle's pass-dependent offense. 

This will be a great, low-scoring game (much like last year's regular-season matchups) that either team could win outright. But since these are two really good teams, I'd suggest taking the 49ers and the points (+3) over the San Francisco Moneyline ( +136 ). 

 Pick: 49ers +3 ( -110 ) 
 

### Las Vegas Raiders vs. New England Patriots 

I can't shake the feeling this line is inflated for the Patriots because Drake Maye and the offense had such a good game against a lackluster Bills defense last week. Maybe they're on track now and just needed one game to shake off the doldrums that had controlled them for the first three weeks. Or maybe they took advantage of Buffalo's questionable defense and an inconsistent day for Josh Allen and the Bills' offense. 

Kirk Cousins and the Raiders have been one of the season's more pleasant surprises so far. Despite a late turnover that gave Kansas City an 11-point lead with three minutes to go, they nearly got into field goal range and had a chance to send the game to overtime. This is not the same old Raiders. It's a team with talent that is well-coached and not folding under pressure. 

They absolutely have a chance to win this one outright, but at the least, they'll stay within three points. 

 Picks: Raiders +3.5 ( -110 ) & Browns Moneyline ( +164 )

<script>
  (function () {
    try {
      const match = document.cookie.match(/(?:^|;\s*)bp_userdata=([^;]*)/);
      let user = null;
      if (match && match[1]) {
        const raw = decodeURIComponent(match[1]).replace(/^"|"$/g, '');
        user = JSON.parse(decodeURIComponent(atob(raw)));
      }
      const level = String((user && user.subscription_level) || '').toLowerCase();
      const premium = level === 'premium' || level === 'goat';
      document.documentElement.setAttribute(
        'data-nav-auth',
        user ? (premium ? 'premium' : 'free') : 'out'
      );

      // Which desktop Upgrade label is coming, because the two are not the same width:
      // the non-trial branch adds a lock icon and a gap before a longer word. Mirrors
      // resolveTrialAudience() — affiliate, then past-trial, else trial — and every input
      // it needs is already in reach here (`bp_affiliate` is its own cookie; the other two
      // are fields on `bp_userdata`). A premium user gets no CTA at all, so no attribute.
      if (!premium) {
        const affiliate =
          /(?:^|;\s*)bp_affiliate=/.test(document.cookie) || Boolean(user && user.affiliate_code);
        const wide = affiliate || Boolean(user && user.has_past_trial);
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-nav-upgrade-label', wide ? 'premium' : 'trial');
      }
    } catch (e) {
      /* leave it unset: every placeholder paints, i.e. the pre-existing behaviour */
    }

    // Separate try/catch, because localStorage throws outright in some privacy modes and a
    // failure here must not cost us the cookie-derived audience above. nav/GetStarted exits
    // on EITHER a signed-in user or this flag, so a logged-out visitor who already finished
    // onboarding gets no CTA and must not be shown a placeholder for one.
    try {
      if (localStorage.getItem('bp_onboarding_completed') === 'true') {
        document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-nav-onboarded', 'true');
      }
    } catch (e) {
      /* same fail-open: no attribute, placeholder paints */
    }
  })();
</script>

<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Injuries</strong></p>
<blockquote class="article-content__blockquote twitter-tweet" data-width="500" data-dnt="true">
<p class="article-content__paragraph" lang="en" dir="ltr"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://x.com/hashtag/Jaguars?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#Jaguars</a> & <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://x.com/hashtag/Eagles?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#Eagles</a> Thursday Injury Report </p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Eric Murray (concussion protocol) upgraded to Limited </p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Quinyon Mitchell upgraded to Full Participant today; Dontayvion Wicks added Thursday with a hamstring <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://t.co/WiG2wHe2QV">pic.twitter.com/WiG2wHe2QV</a></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">— Mia O'Brien (@MiaOBrienTV) <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://x.com/MiaOBrienTV/status/2108301664218218517?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 8, 2026</a></p></blockquote>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Overall</strong></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">So far, I am 2-1 betting on my Jags ATS this season. And when they have delivered as favorites at home, laying points…I’m 2-0. Trust the process. The betting trends strongly support backing DUVAL county as they host a REELING Philly team in London. The Jags are heavy home favorites. Most international games, it doesn’t matter who the actual home team is, but London is the home away from home for Jacksonville, as we all know. So I do think the home trends still hold some weight here.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">This spread has moved a lot since last Sunday, as the <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5O_yW_iE1V0" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Week 5 early lookahead lines show</a>. Hopefully you got in on some Jaguars -4.5.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Before Week 4, it was Jags -2.5, then -4.5, and now hovering at that 7-point mark as the best line on some sportsbooks.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">As I talked about <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/articles/nfl-betting-primer-picks-predictions-week-4-2026/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">last week</a>, favorites tend to dominate the international matchups (the Colts won and covered versus the Washington Commanders in Week 4).</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">So back to favorites as the play. Especially when it’s a Jaguars team that has performed so well in this role since last season.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Per Next Gen Stats: The Jaguars have won 11 of their last 12 regular-season games since Week 11 of the 2025 season. In that span, their 31.1 points per game, 14.1 points per game allowed, and 22 takeaways are all the best in the NFL. Trevor Lawrence has amassed 32 total touchdowns (27 passing, 5 rushing) in that stretch, the most by any player in the NFL.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Jacksonville is 9-3 ATS and straight up at home under Liam Coen across the 2025 regular season, 2025 playoffs, and 2026 to date, including 2-0 at home in 2026 (both ATS and SU). Best home record ATS since Coen became the HC. Also the best ATS record as a favorite (9-2). 6-1 ATS as a home favorite.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Meanwhile, the Eagles keep spiraling. 0-4 ATS this season. They are now 5-11 ATS after a loss since 2023. Worst mark in the NFL.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">And I don’t think it’s getting fixed anytime soon.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The Eagles offense is so broken: per NGS, Philadelphia has a league-leading 15 three-and-out drives this season, with 11 of those coming in the 2nd half. The Eagles have failed to score in the 2nd half over the last two weeks, with their 11 drives resulting in 6 punts, 4 turnovers on downs, and 1 interception. Since the start of the 2025 season, Philadelphia has had a three-and-out on 29.5% of their drives, the highest rate in the NFL.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Then consider all the lost skill position pieces on the offense: Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, and Dallas Goedert – with the offensive line a whole other issue. This team has been a straight auto-fade without stud RT Lane Johnson, who recently announced his retirement. The team also traded away another starter, Cam Jurgens, to the Ravens for future draft capital.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">It should be noted that Jurgens wasn’t playing particularly well after filling in for Landon Dickerson at guard.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Per NGS: Jurgens has allowed 18 pressures, tied for the second-most among interior offensive linemen. Jurgens has allowed pressure on 18.5% of his one-on-one pass blocks, the highest rate among interior offensive linemen (min. 50 one-on-one pass blocks). With Johnson out in Week 4 against the Rams, Markel Bell allowed seven pressures and two sacks on 33 pass blocks, the most pressures allowed by an Eagles lineman in a game this season, as Philadelphia allowed pressure on 19 of 33 dropbacks (57.6%), its highest rate in a game since at least 2018.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">In Week 4, Philadelphia’s offense finished with 172 net yards, a 3.0 yards-per-play average, 4 sacks allowed and a 0-for-12 third-down line - with Saquon Barkley out after two carries and DeVonta Smith/Lane Johnson inactive.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Since 2024, Philadelphia averaged 4.8 yards per carry with Johnson on the field, compared to 4.0 without him. Eagles ball carriers also averaged 2.0 rushing yards before contact per carry with Johnson on the field and 1.3 without him. The Eagles recorded an explosive play on 14.4% of plays with Johnson on the field, a rate that would rank sixth-highest among team seasons since 2024, compared to 11.8% without him, which would rank fifth-lowest.</p>
<blockquote class="article-content__blockquote twitter-tweet" data-width="500" data-dnt="true">
<p class="article-content__paragraph" lang="en" dir="ltr">You've seen repeated references to the Eagles' record without Lane Johnson by now. </p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Want more data about his impact on games? Consider Jalen Hurts' stats with and without Johnson:</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Since 2020, Hurts is No. 8 in the NFL in EPA/dropback with Johnson on the field. He's No. 43 (of...</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">— Zach Berman (@ZBerm) <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://x.com/ZBerm/status/1991247393266729065?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 19, 2025</a></p></blockquote>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">According to <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/ask/jalen-hurts-stats-without-lane-johnson" target="_blank" rel="noopener">StatMuse</a>, Hurts also averages UNDER 175 passing yards per game without Johnson in the lineup. He also averages just 120 passing yards per game in his last 5 games without DeVonta Smith, per FantasyPros’ <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.fantasypros.com/nfl/with-or-without/jalen-hurts?without=devonta-smith" target="_blank" rel="noopener">With or Without You Tool</a>. Take the under on the Eagles QB’s passing yards this week.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The Eagles have allowed pressure on 43.2% of their dropbacks this season, the third-highest rate in the NFL.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">According to <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://x.com/billbarnwell/status/2106770139450372317" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Bill Barnwell</a>, since 2013, across all the various Eagles QBs and their Total QBR…</p>
<ul class="article-content__ul">
<li class="article-content__list-item">With Lane Johnson on the field: 62.5 (3rd-best in the NFL)</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">Without Lane Johnson on the field: 46.8 (29th)</li>
</ul>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The Eagles’ defense has also not carried its weight, either ranking as an elite unit:</p>
<ul class="article-content__ul">
<li class="article-content__list-item">Bottom-10 in EPA/play allowed</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">Bottom-10 in EPA/pass attempt faced</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">6th-worst in EPA/rush faced</li>
</ul>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">They have faced the Commanders, Titans, Bears, and Rams this season.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Fading the Eagles seems obvious, especially when facing a legitimate SB contender in Jacksonville.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Lawrence has averaged 9.0 yards per attempt when facing four or fewer pass rushers this season (2nd-most in the NFL), a defensive tendency the Eagles do 80.1% of the time (3rd-highest) per NGS.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Beyond his yards per attempt, Lawrence has also totaled eight touchdowns (1 INT) against non-blitzes, tied for most in the NFL with Kirk Cousins (2 INT). In total, Lawrence leads the NFL with a 131.3 passer rating against four or fewer pass rushers, the highest by any quarterback in the Next Gen Stats era (since 2016).</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The Jags also boast an underrated defense</p>
<ul class="article-content__ul">
<li class="article-content__list-item">5th best versus the pass (EPA/attempt faced)</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">14th in pressure rate</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">2nd fewest rushing yards allowed per game.</li>
</ul>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The defense has also dominated in the red zone, trailing only the Vikings in red-zone conversion rate (29%). If the Eagles can’t score TDs or sustain drives…this game could get ugly real quick.</p>

<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Overall</strong></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">We have three divisional matchups this week featuring home underdogs: the Packers, Chargers, and Titans. With only one of these teams having won a game so far this season, the Packers are my favorite of the bunch (though I think blindly betting all three is probably the right process play).</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Home underdogs are 14-8-1 ATS. Divisional home underdogs are 5-0 ATS and 4-1 SU, and divisional underdogs overall are 10-2 ATS. Printing press.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Factor in that the Chicago Bears aren’t nearly as profitable ATS on the road as they are at Soldier Field, and that they’re starting a backup QB who threw close to 3 INTs last week, all erased by New York Jets penalties; this is a total lock for me.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The Packers are never a strong bet on the road as favorites, but as home underdogs -> they are 4-2 ATS since 2023. This is only the 7th time they’ve been home underdogs in the last three seasons. And it’s only their second home game after opening the season with 3 of 4 road games.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">GB narrowly escaped Tampa Bay with a 17-14 win. But as I alluded to in my Thursday Night Football Betting Primer, the Pack could have easily won by 10-plus points had it not been for two red-zone turnovers deep in enemy territory.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The Packers have the better and more established QB in this game, so it’s a no-brainer for me. I’m also not convinced the Bears defense has become elite over the last three weeks, given their games against the Vikings (Carson Wentz in bad weather), Eagles (broken), and Jets (ran 32 offensive plays).</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The Packers beat the Bears at home last year by 7 points as 6.5-point favorites. In these 3 GB-CHI matchups last year, the home team won <em>and</em> covered.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Best HC as an underdog ATS in the NFL: Matt LaFleur at 61% (minimum 2 seasons) tied with Houston’s DeMeco Ryans.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">I understand the Packers’ OL woes, but the offense has changed a bit to mitigate the impact. Jordan Love is getting the ball out quickly. Love has averaged 2.48 seconds to throw this season, the quickest mark in the NFL and nearly three-tenths of a second faster than his next-closest qualified-season mark of 2.77 seconds, set in 2023 (Next Gen Stats).</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">And maybe…just maybe…the Packers are more fired up to take a shot on Ben Johnson after he knocked this team out of the playoffs last season…</p>

<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Overall</strong></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The Broncos have the NFL’s worst first-half offense. They have scored one TD in the first half in four games this season, averaging a meager 3.3 PPG in the first half (dead-last). The Chargers? Not much better.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Just 7.5 first-half points per game (27th).</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">And that was before the Los Angeles Chargers suffered more offensive-line injuries. Two starting tackles are likely out for Week 5: Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater. Chargers No. 1 WR Ladd McConkey also re-injured his foot last week.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">So even though the Denver Broncos are down two starting CBs, Pat Surtain and Riley Moss, coverage matters less when the QB doesn’t have time to throw. I think both defenses (even Denver minus their CBs) have trench advantages.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The Bolts defense actually played half-way decent last week.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">In Week 4 versus Seattle, they finished 8th in EPA/play allowed, 10th in yards/play, and generated the 3rd-highest QB pressure rate. Seattle went just 3-for-12 on third downs. The Chargers now rank 7th in pressure rate on the season.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Both defenses also rank top-12 in red-zone conversion rate.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The Chargers are also clearly the worst offense Denver has faced so far this season (KC, JAX, LAR, SF), and only one of those games has surpassed 41 total points.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Overall, both teams are 1-3 toward the Over this season, and their eight combined games have gone <em>6-2</em> toward the Under. Both teams are 0-2 toward the total in their respective home/road roles.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The last time these two teams met in Week 18 of 2025, the total stayed under 42.5 points. In their first matchup played in LA last year, the final score was 23-20 (went under the 45.5-point total).</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">League-wide so far through 2026: closing line totals of 42 or less are only 8-5 Under.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">My official best bet is under in the first half…but I think both the first half and full game total under are firmly in play.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Update: On Thursday, it was confirmed that HC Sean Payton would reclaim play-calling duties to jump-start the offense. But let’s add the context about how it might not just be on OC Davis Webb for the lack of slow starts. Denver was middle of the pack in first-half points scored LAST season. And they had all those second-half comebacks because they were constantly behind in games LAST season, when Payton was still calling plays. I, for one, believe this sluggish offense is a Bo Nix problem. Not aggressive enough downfield to generate explosives. I could see a scenario where Denver scores on their first possession but then goes super conservative versus an offense missing its two starting tackles.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">I already labeled Broncos-Chargers first half as one of my best bets this week before the play-calling switch. Definitely don’t love it. So an interesting hedge if you are having second thoughts…Broncos to score on first drive is +114 odds (any points count). They get into the red zone on a big pass play because Payton is sick of his offense not scoring in the first half…but then they stall out in the red zone and settle for 3.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Let’s have our cake (wedding cake obviously) and eat it too.</p>

<p class="article-content__paragraph">This game feels much more like a stay-away spot for me, given the Commanders are also coming off an international game without a bye week. So far in 2026…those teams (Rams, 49ers, Ravens, Cowboys) are 4-0 S and 3-1 ATS.</p>

<p class="article-content__paragraph">Najee Harris has been the No. 2 RB for the Giants the last two weeks, but there have been some coach-speak rumblings about potentially getting Devin Singletary more involved this week after being a healthy scratch Weeks 2-3. <p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Overall</strong></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">This is a really interesting matchup, with Klint Kubiak and Mike Vrabel meeting again for the first time since the Super Bowl, when Kubiak was Seattle’s offensive coordinator. The Raiders offense has looked really good under Kubiak with Kirk Cousins at quarterback, and even in a loss to the Chiefs, they showed they can hang with the big boys, which was a question mark for a lot of people, myself included. Now they go on the road to take on the Patriots, and this is another test.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">I’ll admit I’m a bit of a homer here, but I like the Patriots at this number. Eventually, I think Kirk Cousins is going to start to tail off. I just don’t think what he’s doing is sustainable at a 17-game pace, though I may be off base.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">How the Raiders’ defense plays against the Patriots’ offense will be the telltale sign. The Vegas defense has been underrated all season (5th in EPA/play allowed). If it shows out, this could turn into an Under and a spot to bet against Cousins continuing at an elite level and against Drake Maye when he faces a better defense (unlike last week versus a reeling Bills’ defense).</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Full disclosure: I have been on point with the Patriots the last two weeks: I bet them to get boat-raced by the Jags, and I covered the spread last week at Buffalo. This matchup, though, I have much less confidence in how the game will go. Which naturally means it’s a lock for the Pats to win by 3 or 4 points – giving me zero sense of a strong reason to bet on this contest.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Even so, betting on the Pats blindly at home as strong favorites has been the profitable trend. Either the Pats laying the points… or the game total UNDER 45. But even the total feels shaky given the Pats are down 3 CBs…making it seem like another strong outing in the future for the Raiders veteran QB. That is…if the Raiders WR room can take advantage.</p>

<li class="article-content__list-item">Houston’s last 4 road division games have all gone Under.</li>
</ul>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Injuries</strong></p>
<blockquote class="article-content__blockquote twitter-tweet" data-width="500" data-dnt="true">
<p class="article-content__paragraph" lang="en" dir="ltr"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://x.com/hashtag/Titans?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#Titans</a> injury report for Thursday ahead of Sunday vs the Texans with update from Houston. <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://t.co/E7dllekgEA">pic.twitter.com/E7dllekgEA</a></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">— TURRON DAVENPORT (@TDavenport_NFL) <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://x.com/TDavenport_NFL/status/2108314373483630605?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 8, 2026</a></p></blockquote>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Overall</strong></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">This line screams to me: Texans win, but the Titans cover the 7.5. Both teams are winless, which makes a touchdown-plus a bit generous for Houston (who is also 0-4 ATS this season). Home divisional underdogs have been cooking this year, so that, along with the under (Texans defense + Titans offense), seems like the no-brainer way to attack this AFC South matchup.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Houston’s defense should have its best game to date, since the Titans are by far the worst offense they have faced all season (BUF, CIN, IND, DAL). HC DeMeco Ryans has also taken back defensive play-calling duties.</p>
<hr />
<h3 class="article-content__subheading"><strong>San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks</strong></h3>
<h3 class="article-content__subheading">Betting Lines & Odds</h3>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><iframe height="250px" style="width: 100%;" frameborder="0" src="https://www.bettingpros.com/widgets/matchup-widget.php?sport=NFL&eventid=21943&marketid=3:2:1"></iframe></p>
<h3 class="article-content__subheading">Erickson’s Pick: Under 46.5</h3>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Trends</strong></p>
<ul class="article-content__ul">
<li class="article-content__list-item">SF has not yet played as a road underdog in 2026 (through Week 4). Overall: no non-neutral road games yet; as an underdog, 1-0 ATS and 0-1 O/U; in all 2026 games, 3-1 ATS and 2-2 O/U.</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">As a home favorite, SEA is 0-0-2 ATS and 1-1 O/U in 2026. Overall: across all home games, 0-0-2 ATS and 1-1 O/U; across all games as a favorite, 1-1-2 ATS and 2-2 O/U; across all 2026 games, 1-1-2 ATS and 2-2 O/U.</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">SF streaks through Week 4: 4-0 straight up (4-game win streak), 3-1 against the spread (1-game cover streak), 2-2 toward the total (1-game Under streak).</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">SEA streaks through Week 4: 3-1 straight up (1-game win streak), 1-1-2 against the spread (1-game non-cover streak), 2-2 toward the total (2-game Over streak).</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">Seattle is 15-8-3 ATS as a favorite (includes the Week 4 push at -7 against the Chargers).</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">Seattle has won 9 straight home games, dating back to the 2025 season.</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">Seattle is 7-1 ATS in its last 8 NFC West games since the 2025 season.</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">Seattle’s last four home division games have all gone Over since the 2025 season.</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">Seattle is 8-4 at home toward the over since the start of last season.</li>
</ul>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Injuries</strong></p>
<blockquote class="article-content__blockquote twitter-tweet" data-width="500" data-dnt="true">
<p class="article-content__paragraph" lang="en" dir="ltr">Seahawks vs. 49ers injury report for Thursday: <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://t.co/eE8VDbTL0c">pic.twitter.com/eE8VDbTL0c</a></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">— John Boyle (@johnpboyle) <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://x.com/johnpboyle/status/2108330078312845590?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 8, 2026</a></p></blockquote>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Overall</strong></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">This is the game I’m probably most excited about on the slate. It’s a divisional matchup, NFC West, two juggernaut teams. The 49ers are undefeated, and the Seahawks are trying to knock them off as the reigning Super Bowl champions.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">I don’t have a lean here, but Seth Woolcock loves the under as one of his best bets of the week. In their three matchups last season, the scores were 13-17, 41-6, and 13-3.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><div class="article-content__div yt-embed-container"><iframe loading="lazy" title="10 BEST BETS for NFL Week 5: Top Picks & Predictions to Make NOW (2026)" width="500" height="281" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/2-fTrFRuxNw?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe></div></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">The 49ers’ offense did come down to Earth last week against a tougher Broncos defense, so we could see something similar on the road against Seattle.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Emanuel Wilson has taken on a bigger role in the Seahawks’ backfield after Jadarian Price’s injury. But I do question his monster rushing+receiving yards line in Week 5 at a whopping 79.5 yards. The 49ers defense has allowed the 6th-fewest combined rushing+receiving yards to RBs this season – even with the recent strong performances from RJ Harvey (all receiving), Jeremiyah Love, and De’Von Achane.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Last week, Wilson had two carries for 15-yard gains, whereas on his other 19 carries he averaged just 2.7 yards per clip (19 for 51). His efficiency has been modest at best, and his 3 catches for 39 yards (23 on one catch) don’t seem sustainable, especially with George Holani heavily involved as a receiver out of the backfield. He’s a volume bet for sure…but Seattle controlling the ball and tempo against the Niners isn’t as much of a guarantee.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Among qualified rushers, Wilson ranks in the bottom-20 in success rate, yards per carry, and EPA/attempt.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">I’m also hesitant to call any matchup against a defense led by linebacker Fred Warner great for an opposing RB. Per Next Gen Stats… Warner has recorded a tackle in the run game on a career-high 26.9% of snaps this season, the third-highest rate among off-ball linebackers with at least 50 snaps in run defense, trailing only Azeez Al-Shaair (28.1%) and Alex Singleton (27.7%). Warner has also missed only one tackle in run defense, while Al-Shaair and Singleton have missed two and five tackles, respectively. As a defense, the 49ers have a 11.0% missed-tackle rate on called-run plays, the sixth-lowest in the NFL.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">SF is allowing just 3.7 YPC this season. 5-star BET on the Prop Bet Cheat Sheet this week.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">That’s where I will stop betting unders in this game. Seattle loves to give up RB production in the passing game, so I think this is a spot where Christian McCaffrey gets peppered with targets. His catches have gone down in four straight weeks (5, 4, 4, 3), but so much of that has been game-script-related. In a more back-and-forth contest, I think he stays more involved for all four quarters. Besides, in his last 3 games versus Seattle…he has 9, 6, and 5 catches…all hitting the over on 4.5.</p>
<h3 class="article-content__subheading">Props</h3>
<ul class="article-content__ul">
<li class="article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/emanuel-wilson/rushing-receiving-yards/"><strong>Emanuel Wilson UNDER 79.5 rushing and receiving yards</strong></a></li>
<li class="article-content__list-item"><a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://www.bettingpros.com/nfl/props/christian-mccaffrey/receptions/"><strong>Christian McCaffrey OVER 4.5 receptions</strong></a></li>
</ul>
<hr />
<h3 class="article-content__subheading"><strong>Baltimore Ravens at Atlanta Falcons</strong></h3>
<h3 class="article-content__subheading">Betting Lines & Odds</h3>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><iframe height="250px" style="width: 100%;" frameborder="0" src="https://www.bettingpros.com/widgets/matchup-widget.php?sport=NFL&eventid=21945&marketid=3:2:1"></iframe></p>
<h3 class="article-content__subheading">Erickson’s Pick: Over 43.5</h3>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Trends</strong></p>
<ul class="article-content__ul">
<li class="article-content__list-item">BAL has not yet played as a road underdog in 2026 (through Week 4). Overall: across all road games, 1-0 ATS and 1-0 O/U; no games yet as an underdog; across all 2026 games, 1-2-1 ATS and 2-2 O/U.</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">ATL has not yet played as a home favorite in 2026 (through Week 4). Overall: 0-1 ATS and 0-1 O/U across all home games; no games as a favorite yet; 2-2 ATS and 2-2 O/U across all 2026 games.</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">BAL streaks through Week 4: 3-1 straight up (2-game win streak), 1-2-1 against the spread (2-game non-cover streak), 2-2 toward the total (1-game Under streak).</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">ATL streaks through Week 4: 2-2 straight up (2-game win streak), 2-2 against the spread (2-game cover streak), 2-2 toward the total (2-game Over streak).</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">Baltimore is 2-8 or 3-7 ATS in its last 10 games (including the 2025 season), after failing to cover as an 11.5-point home favorite in Week 4.</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">Baltimore has gone Over the total in 5 of its last 6 games (5-1).</li>
<li class="article-content__list-item">Atlanta is 1-5 ATS in its last 6 home games, dating back to the 2025 season.</li>
</ul>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Injuries</strong></p>
<blockquote class="article-content__blockquote twitter-tweet" data-width="500" data-dnt="true">
<p class="article-content__paragraph" lang="en" dir="ltr">Ravens' Thursday injury report:</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Lamar Jackson indeed did not practice for a second straight day.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">WR Zay Flowers (foot) was limited for a second straight day.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Ronnie Stanley (toe/ankle) was a full practice participant.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Kyle Hamilton (groin) was also full, along with Rashod... <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://t.co/meSkRHW7OD">pic.twitter.com/meSkRHW7OD</a></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">— Ryan Mink (@ryanmink) <a class="article-content__anchor" href="https://x.com/ryanmink/status/2108286817162191079?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 8, 2026</a></p></blockquote>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph"><strong>Overall</strong></p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">No Lamar Jackson. If the Ravens organization learned anything last year, it’s that when he returned without being fully healthy, it was a disaster, and you can’t let that happen again. You give him as many weeks as humanly possible, because you need to get back to a 100 percent healthy Lamar Jackson or you compromise the season.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Tyler Huntley has been productive in the Lamar role before, so he can at least right the ship in the meantime while featuring Derrick Henry a ton.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">But this is a tough draw for the Ravens RB versus the No. 1 run defense in rushing yards allowed per game. The Ravens were also extremely banged up across their interior OL, which is why they traded for center Cam Jurgens.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">On the Falcons’ side, this feels like a natural flat spot. Third prime-time game in a row. Home favorites versus a backup QB. Two great offensive performances in back-to-back weeks. But there’s nobody on the defense who can stop Zay Flowers. And as we saw Thursday night with Jalen Hurts, plucky mobile QBs can terrorize defenses. With the Ravens’ star pass rusher Trey Hendrickson also out…I like the game total over the best in this matchup.</p>
<p class="article-content__paragraph">Huntley’s last 3 starts have all gone over the projected game totals.</p>

### Philadelphia Eagles at Jacksonville Jaguars 

### Betting Lines & Odds

 

### Erickson's Pick: Jaguars -7

 Trends 
 

- PHI has not yet played as a road underdog in 2026 (through Week 4). Overall: across all road games, 0-2 ATS and 1-1 O/U; across all underdog games, 0-1 ATS and 1-0 O/U; across all 2026 games, 0-4 ATS and 3-1 O/U.

- PHI streaks through Week 4: 2-2 straight up (2-game losing streak), 0-4 against the spread (4-game non-cover streak), 3-1 toward the total (1-game Over streak). 

- JAX streaks through Week 4: 3-1 straight up (2-game win streak), 3-1 against the spread (2-game cover streak), 1-3 toward the total (3-game Under streak). 

- Philadelphia is 12-8 ATS on the road from 2024 through 2026. 

- Philadelphia has gone Under in 7 or 8 of its last 12 games (7-5 or 8-4), dating back to the 2025 season, but 3 of its 4 games in 2026 have gone Over. 

- Jacksonville is 11-2 in its last 13 games, dating back to the 2025 season. 

- Jacksonville is 9-3 ATS and straight up at home under Liam Coen across the 2025 regular season, 2025 playoffs, and 2026 to date, including 2-0 at home in 2026 (both ATS and SU). 

- Best home record ATS since Coen became the HC. Also the best ATS record as a favorite (9-2). 6-1 ATS as a home favorite. 

- The Eagles have won 6 of their last 7 games as an underdog, dating back to the 2025 season. 

- The Eagles are 7-point underdogs for the first time since 2021 ( Sheil Kapadia ) - also the last time Philly had a losing record. 

- Jacksonville is 3-2 straight up and ATS in London in the last three seasons. 

- So far in 2026, the international games are 1-2 toward the O/U. 

- Seven of the last 13 international games have gone OVER the total. 

- Eleven of the last 18 international games have gone UNDER the total. 

- Per Covers.com: Favorites are 49-17 straight up (SU) and 41-24-1 against the spread (ATS) for a 63% hit rate. The O/U is 30-36 (45%). 
 

 Injuries 
 

 #Jaguars & #Eagles Thursday Injury Report

Quinyon Mitchell upgraded to Full Participant today; Dontayvion Wicks added Thursday with a hamstring pic.twitter.com/WiG2wHe2QV 

 Mia O'Brien (@MiaOBrienTV) October 8, 2026 

 

 Overall 

So far, I am 2-1 betting on my Jags ATS this season. And when they have delivered as favorites at home, laying points…I'm 2-0. Trust the process. The betting trends strongly support backing DUVAL county as they host a REELING Philly team in London. The Jags are heavy home favorites. Most international games, it doesn't matter who the actual home team is, but London is the home away from home for Jacksonville, as we all know. So I do think the home trends still hold some weight here. 

This spread has moved a lot since last Sunday, as the Week 5 early lookahead lines show . Hopefully you got in on some Jaguars -4.5. 

Before Week 4, it was Jags -2.5, then -4.5, and now hovering at that 7-point mark as the best line on some sportsbooks. 

As I talked about last week , favorites tend to dominate the international matchups (the Colts won and covered versus the Washington Commanders in Week 4). 

So back to favorites as the play. Especially when it's a Jaguars team that has performed so well in this role since last season. 

Per Next Gen Stats: The Jaguars have won 11 of their last 12 regular-season games since Week 11 of the 2025 season. In that span, their 31.1 points per game, 14.1 points per game allowed, and 22 takeaways are all the best in the NFL. Trevor Lawrence has amassed 32 total touchdowns (27 passing, 5 rushing) in that stretch, the most by any player in the NFL. 

Jacksonville is 9-3 ATS and straight up at home under Liam Coen across the 2025 regular season, 2025 playoffs, and 2026 to date, including 2-0 at home in 2026 (both ATS and SU). Best home record ATS since Coen became the HC. Also the best ATS record as a favorite (9-2). 6-1 ATS as a home favorite. 

Meanwhile, the Eagles keep spiraling. 0-4 ATS this season. They are now 5-11 ATS after a loss since 2023. Worst mark in the NFL. 

And I don't think it's getting fixed anytime soon. 

The Eagles offense is so broken: per NGS, Philadelphia has a league-leading 15 three-and-out drives this season, with 11 of those coming in the 2nd half. The Eagles have failed to score in the 2nd half over the last two weeks, with their 11 drives resulting in 6 punts, 4 turnovers on downs, and 1 interception. Since the start of the 2025 season, Philadelphia has had a three-and-out on 29.5% of their drives, the highest rate in the NFL. 

Then consider all the lost skill position pieces on the offense: Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, and Dallas Goedert - with the offensive line a whole other issue. This team has been a straight auto-fade without stud RT Lane Johnson, who recently announced his retirement. The team also traded away another starter, Cam Jurgens, to the Ravens for future draft capital. 

It should be noted that Jurgens wasn't playing particularly well after filling in for Landon Dickerson at guard. 

Per NGS: Jurgens has allowed 18 pressures, tied for the second-most among interior offensive linemen. Jurgens has allowed pressure on 18.5% of his one-on-one pass blocks, the highest rate among interior offensive linemen (min. 50 one-on-one pass blocks). With Johnson out in Week 4 against the Rams, Markel Bell allowed seven pressures and two sacks on 33 pass blocks, the most pressures allowed by an Eagles lineman in a game this season, as Philadelphia allowed pressure on 19 of 33 dropbacks (57.6%), its highest rate in a game since at least 2018. 

In Week 4, Philadelphia's offense finished with 172 net yards, a 3.0 yards-per-play average, 4 sacks allowed and a 0-for-12 third-down line - with Saquon Barkley out after two carries and DeVonta Smith/Lane Johnson inactive. 

Since 2024, Philadelphia averaged 4.8 yards per carry with Johnson on the field, compared to 4.0 without him. Eagles ball carriers also averaged 2.0 rushing yards before contact per carry with Johnson on the field and 1.3 without him. The Eagles recorded an explosive play on 14.4% of plays with Johnson on the field, a rate that would rank sixth-highest among team seasons since 2024, compared to 11.8% without him, which would rank fifth-lowest. 
 

You've seen repeated references to the Eagles' record without Lane Johnson by now. 

Want more data about his impact on games? Consider Jalen Hurts' stats with and without Johnson:

 Zach Berman (@ZBerm) November 19, 2025 

 

According to StatMuse , Hurts also averages UNDER 175 passing yards per game without Johnson in the lineup. He also averages just 120 passing yards per game in his last 5 games without DeVonta Smith, per FantasyPros' With or Without You Tool . Take the under on the Eagles QB's passing yards this week. 

The Eagles have allowed pressure on 43.2% of their dropbacks this season, the third-highest rate in the NFL. 

According to Bill Barnwell , since 2013, across all the various Eagles QBs and their Total QBR… 
 

- With Lane Johnson on the field: 62.5 (3rd-best in the NFL) 

- Without Lane Johnson on the field: 46.8 (29th) 
 

The Eagles' defense has also not carried its weight, either ranking as an elite unit: 
 

- Bottom-10 in EPA/play allowed 

- Bottom-10 in EPA/pass attempt faced 

- 6th-worst in EPA/rush faced 
 

They have faced the Commanders, Titans, Bears, and Rams this season. 

Fading the Eagles seems obvious, especially when facing a legitimate SB contender in Jacksonville. 

Lawrence has averaged 9.0 yards per attempt when facing four or fewer pass rushers this season (2nd-most in the NFL), a defensive tendency the Eagles do 80.1% of the time (3rd-highest) per NGS. 

Beyond his yards per attempt, Lawrence has also totaled eight touchdowns (1 INT) against non-blitzes, tied for most in the NFL with Kirk Cousins (2 INT). In total, Lawrence leads the NFL with a 131.3 passer rating against four or fewer pass rushers, the highest by any quarterback in the Next Gen Stats era (since 2016). 

The Jags also boast an underrated defense 
 

- 5th best versus the pass (EPA/attempt faced) 

- 14th in pressure rate 

- 2nd fewest rushing yards allowed per game. 
 

The defense has also dominated in the red zone, trailing only the Vikings in red-zone conversion rate (29%). If the Eagles can't score TDs or sustain drives…this game could get ugly real quick.

### Chicago Bears at Green Bay Packers 

### Betting Lines & Odds

 

### Erickson's Pick: Packers +2.5

 Trends 
 

- As a road favorite, CHI is 1-0 ATS (100%) and 1-0 O/U in 2026. Overall: across all road games, 1-0 ATS and 1-0 O/U; as a favorite, 2-1 ATS and 1-2 O/U; in 2026, 3-1 ATS and 1-3 O/U.

Packers-Bears Thursday injury report pic.twitter.com/g3KtT56vqF

We have three divisional matchups this week featuring home underdogs: the Packers, Chargers, and Titans. With only one of these teams having won a game so far this season, the Packers are my favorite of the bunch (though I think blindly betting all three is probably the right process play).

GB narrowly escaped Tampa Bay with a 17-14 win. But as I alluded to in my Thursday Night Football Betting Primer, the Pack could have easily won by 10-plus points had it not been for two red-zone turnovers deep in enemy territory.

I'm also not convinced the Bears defense has become elite over the last three weeks, given their games against the Vikings (Carson Wentz in bad weather), Eagles (broken), and Jets (ran 32 offensive plays). 

The Packers beat the Bears at home last year by 7 points as 6.5-point favorites. In these 3 GB-CHI matchups last year, the home team won and covered. 

Best HC as an underdog ATS in the NFL: Matt LaFleur at 61% (minimum 2 seasons) tied with Houston's DeMeco Ryans. 

I understand the Packers' OL woes, but the offense has changed a bit to mitigate the impact. Jordan Love is getting the ball out quickly. Love has averaged 2.48 seconds to throw this season, the quickest mark in the NFL and nearly three-tenths of a second faster than his next-closest qualified-season mark of 2.77 seconds, set in 2023 (Next Gen Stats). 

And maybe…just maybe…the Packers are more fired up to take a shot on Ben Johnson after he knocked this team out of the playoffs last season…
